item.title: Central rivals Blues, Predators aim to keep building
item.description: Two teams looking to climb the Central Division standings will face off Saturday in Nashville, when the Predators host the St. Louis Blues.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Two teams looking to climb the Central Division standings will face off Saturday in Nashville, when the Predators host the St. Louis Blues. The Blues will wrap up a three-game road trip after they lost 5-4 to the Minnesota Wild on Thursday night. St. Louis scored twice in the final four minutes, including a short-handed goal by Robert Thomas, but coach Jim Montgomery's team could not complete the comeback to force overtime. "Well, 1-1 on a three-game road trip, we got to come out above .500," Montgomery said. "We'll get on the plane, get to Nashville, have a really good practice (Friday) and come out Saturday night with a little more determined effort than we had (Thursday)." Nashville, though, did force the extra session on Thursday. The Predators overcame a 2-0 deficit to San Jose midway through the third period and earned a point thanks to Steven Stamkos' last-second goal, which tied the contest. The Sharks prevailed in the shootout, extending Nashville's winless streak to three games (0-1-2). Nashville has leaned on its veterans, with all five of its leading scorers at least 32 years old. Stamkos, 36, leads the team with four goals and eight points. A two-time Stanley Cup winner with Tampa Bay, Stamkos is now in his third year with Nashville, which has only made the playoffs once in the last four seasons. "I think we're very well aware of where we want to be and how we want to begin the year," coach Andrew Brunette said. "So, I think we're putting a little bit added pressure on ourselves. For sure there's disappointment (with the overtime loss), but we just pick ourselves up and go back to work. You stacked a point out of it, and you build to the next game." Goalie Juuse Saros (2-2-2, 2.95 goals-against average), another Predators veteran, has started six of the team's seven games and stopped 30 shots in the loss to San Jose. The Finnish netminder has allowed just 18 of 187 shots, posting a .904 save percentage. Saros has faced the Blues 24 times over his 12 NHL seasons. He's 10-11-2 with a 3.36 GAA and an .885 save percentage. Nashville may get Mavrik Bourque back in the lineup. The 24-year-old center, acquired in July from the Dallas Stars, has missed the past week due to an upper-body injury, but he was on the ice for practice Friday. St. Louis had its two-game winning streak snapped Thursday, but the Blues have improved offensively, scoring 16 goals over their past three games. Mason McTavish, acquired from Anaheim in June, leads the Blues with five goals and eight points. The 23-year-old center has a five-game point streak, including three goals and an assist in his past two contests. Netminder Joel Hofer (2-2-1, 2.43 GAA) has started both games on the road trip. In eight career games against Nashville, Hofer, 26, is 4-3-0 with a 3.59 GAA and an .865 save percentage. Pavel Buchnevich, who had three assists in the 7-2 win over Ottawa on Tuesday, missed Thursday's game against the Wild due to the birth of his child. It's unclear whether he'll return for Saturday's game. --Field Level Media

item.title: Experts divided on whether Dodgers' sweep shifts MLB salary cap fight
item.description: Experts are divided over whether the Los Angeles Dodgers' sweep by the Milwaukee Brewers in the National League Championship Series will affect Major League Baseball's labor talks, where owners are pushing for a salary cap that players oppose.
item.dc:creator: Rory Carroll
item.content:encoded: Experts are divided over whether the Los Angeles Dodgers' sweep by the Milwaukee Brewers in the National League Championship Series will affect Major League Baseball's labor talks, where owners are pushing for a salary cap that players oppose. The big-spending Dodgers were thoroughly outplayed by the relentless Brewers, who rank 19th in payroll out of the league's 30 clubs. Milwaukee will return to the World Series for the first time in 44 years after vanquishing the two-time defending champions. Tony Torain, a partner at McDermott Will & Schulte who specializes in labor and employment law, said the result weakens the owners' case that there isn't enough parity in the sport. "I think we'll have a lockout and the league will still try to use that leverage," he said. "But in terms of making the argument for why they think they need a salary cap, the Brewers undercut it. There's definitely leverage on the PA's side," he said, referring to the players' association. He said the union will argue that player development, not payroll, drives winning. He also expects the union to press for higher minimum salaries, an idea it raised early in talks. In their first proposal in May, MLB owners asked for a hard cap of $245.3 million, including player benefits, and a payroll floor of $171.2 million, starting in 2027. The players have long opposed any form of salary cap. The current collective bargaining agreement expires on December 1. Torain said baseball's growing popularity puts added pressure on owners, who have never had a cap in the sport's history. The last time owners pushed for a cap, players went on strike in 1994. The 232-day stoppage forced the cancellation of that year's World Series. "If you have a lockout, it's not on TV, you can't go to the parks, so you're not getting those revenue sources," he said. MESSAGING WIN Bob Dorfman, a San Francisco-based sports marketing analyst, said the Dodgers' playoff exit will change little. "I don't think it's going to change anything that happens for those CBA talks," he said. At most, he said, the sweep is "a messaging win" for the union. He also questioned whether a cap would improve competitive balance, saying attendance, which has risen four seasons in a row, and viewership are strong without one. He agreed that a lockout is likely when the current agreement expires. He said he hopes a stoppage is short, but in a worst case the season could shrink to 70 to 80 games. He said he hopes owners will eventually put off the cap fight for a future contract negotiation. Dorfman said a lockout would anger fans and expects games to be lost, perhaps for a month or two in an optimistic scenario. He said owners tend to win labor fights because they can outlast unions. When reminded that owners failed to win a cap in 1994-95 season, he said, "I hope that happens again."

item.title: Trump zomba da popularidade do nome Mohammad, comum entre os muçulmanos
item.description: O presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, fez uma piada sobre a popularidade do nome Mohammad no mundo muçulmano ao zombar da presidência do Irã durante um discurso de campanha nesta sexta-feira.
item.dc:creator: Steve Holland, Kanishka Singh
item.content:encoded: O presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, fez uma piada sobre a popularidade do nome Mohammad no mundo muçulmano ao zombar da presidência do Irã durante um discurso de campanha nesta sexta-feira. “Sabe, se você tiver dúvidas sobre o nome de alguém do Oriente Médio, basta dizer ‘Mohammad’”, disse Trump à multidão em Dalton, na Geórgia. “Você tem cerca de 65% de chance de acertar. ‘Olá, Mohammad.’ Faço isso há anos. Nunca errei.” Mohammad é um dos nomes masculinos mais comuns entre os muçulmanos, que costumam dar aos filhos o nome do profeta Mohammad, fundador do Islã, conhecido como Maomé no Brasil. Trump fez o comentário enquanto discutia o Irã durante um comício em um hangar no Aeroporto Municipal de Dalton, na Geórgia, onde fez campanha para candidatos republicanos antes das eleições de meio de mandato de 3 de novembro. “O Irã é o único país onde ninguém quer ser presidente”, disse Trump, e então fingiu perguntar a várias pessoas chamadas Mohammad se elas queriam o cargo. Masoud Pezeshkian é presidente do Irã desde 2024. A plateia da Geórgia reagiu com silêncio à piada. Defensores dos direitos humanos e grupos de defesa dos muçulmanos têm criticado repetidamente Trump por uma retórica que, segundo eles, demoniza e ridiculariza muçulmanos, imigrantes e minorias étnicas. Ele intensificou essa retórica durante a campanha para as eleições de meio de mandato, particularmente contra somalis e muçulmanos norte-americanos, incluindo o candidato democrata muçulmano ao Senado dos EUA Abdul El-Sayed e a deputada Ilhan Omar, uma democrata de Minnesota que chegou aos EUA como refugiada somali. Trump reiterou sua promessa de que o Irã nunca teria uma arma nuclear, sete meses depois que os Estados Unidos e Israel lançaram uma guerra contra Teerã com o objetivo, em parte, de paralisar seu programa nuclear. Um relatório anual do Conselho de Relações Islâmico-Americanas, divulgado no início deste ano, atribuiu o aumento da islamofobia nos EUA, em parte, à repressão de Trump à imigração e aos protestos pró-palestinos durante seu segundo mandato.

item.title: EEUU levanta restricciones a aerolíneas mexicanas tras disputa en sector aviación
item.description: Las aerolíneas mexicanas podrán abrir nuevos vuelos a Estados Unidos desde los dos aeropuertos internacionales de Ciudad de México, después de que el Departamento de Transporte de Estados Unidos (DOT por su sigla en inglés) levantara las restricciones impuestas a raíz de las disputas en materia de aviación entre ambos países, dijo el viernes el gobierno mexicano.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Las aerolíneas mexicanas podrán abrir nuevos vuelos a Estados Unidos desde los dos aeropuertos internacionales de Ciudad de México, después de que el Departamento de Transporte de Estados Unidos (DOT por su sigla en inglés) levantara las restricciones impuestas a raíz de las disputas en materia de aviación entre ambos países, dijo el viernes el gobierno mexicano. La decisión permite a las aerolíneas establecer rutas hacia Estados Unidos desde el Aeropuerto Internacional Felipe Ángeles (AIFA) y el Aeropuerto Internacional Benito Juárez de Ciudad de México (AICM), de acuerdo con un comunicado conjunto de las secretarías de Relaciones Exteriores y de Comunicaciones y Transportes. El DOT afirmó que esta medida reflejaba los pasos dados por México para abordar las preocupaciones sobre su cumplimiento de un acuerdo bilateral de transporte aéreo de 2015. El departamento señaló que seguiría exigiendo a las compañías aéreas mexicanas que presentaran los horarios de los vuelos con origen y destino en Estados Unidos y que obtuvieran la autorización para operar servicios con aeronaves de gran tamaño. Un funcionario estadounidense señaló que siguen vigentes otras dos órdenes relacionadas con la controversia y que Washington supervisará de cerca el cumplimiento por parte de México de sus compromisos. El funcionario indicó que la decisión era independiente de una revisión en curso de la Administración Federal de Aviación (FAA por su sigla en inglés) sobre las medidas de supervisión de la aviación en México, llevada a cabo en agosto. La FAA restableció la máxima calificación de seguridad aérea de México en septiembre de 2023, lo que permitió a las aerolíneas mexicanas ampliar las rutas existentes hacia Estados Unidos y poner en marcha nuevos servicios. México había sido degradado en mayo de 2021 después de que el regulador estadounidense determinara que el país no cumplía con las normas internacionales de seguridad aérea. La degradación supuso un duro golpe para las aerolíneas mexicanas, ya que las aerolíneas estadounidenses pudieron hacerse con cuota de mercado. En mayo, el[USN:L6N41I15D TEXT:" secretario de Transporte estadounidense"], Sean Duffy, afirmó que el gobierno mexicano había acordado mejorar el acceso aéreo a Ciudad de México. La administración del presidente estadounidense, Donald Trump, había llegado a un acuerdo con México sobre un plan para abordar las preocupaciones de Estados Unidos respecto al cumplimiento de un acuerdo de transporte aéreo de 2015 entre ambos países, afirmó Duffy. En [USN:L6N3W918R TEXT:"octubre del año pasado"], Estados Unidos congeló la expansión de los servicios de pasajeros y carga de las aerolíneas mexicanas desde esos dos aeropuertos, alegando que México no había cumplido el acuerdo bilateral de aviación desde 2022, cuando rescindió las franjas horarias de las aerolíneas de pasajeros estadounidenses y obligó a las compañías aéreas estadounidenses dedicadas exclusivamente al transporte de carga a trasladar sus operaciones. La decisión del viernes fue bien recibida por las aerolíneas mexicanas; las compañías Viva y Aeroméxico (AERO.MX) señalaron que reforzaría la conectividad aérea entre ambos países.

item.title: Ukraine-La Moldavie blâme la Russie après que des drones s'écrasent sur son territoire
item.description: Les autorités moldaves ont identifié cinq drones qui se sont écrasé sur son territoire comme étant russes, blâmant vendredi Moscou pour ces incidents.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Les autorités moldaves ont identifié cinq drones qui se sont écrasé sur son territoire comme étant russes, blâmant vendredi Moscou pour ces incidents. Le gouvernement moldave pro-européen, qui espère rejoindre l'Union européenne (UE) d'ici 2030, a critiqué à plusieurs reprises l'invasion de l'Ukraine par la Russie, et a dénoncé des incursions dans son espace aérien. La Moldavie est frontalière de l'Ukraine. Les cinq drones ont pénétré jeudi et vendredi dans l'espace aérien moldave et se sont écrasés sur son territoire, essentiellement dans le nord et l'est du pays, blessant légèrement une personne et provoquant des dégâts. "Ces incidents représentent une menace pour la sécurité de nos citoyens et montre les conséquences directes de la guerre agressive de la Russie contre l'Ukraine sur la stabilité de la région", a dit le ministère moldave des Affaires étrangères dans un communiqué. Le ministère a convoqué l'ambassadeur de Russie en Moldavie, Oleg Ozerov, afin de lui demander des explications après ces incidents.

item.title: Trump mocks popularity of the name Mohammad, common among Muslims
item.description: He made a joke about the popularity of the name Mohammad in the Muslim world as he mocked Iran's presidency during a campaign speech.
item.dc:creator: Steve Holland, Kanishka Singh
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump made a joke about the popularity of the name Mohammad in the Muslim world as he mocked Iran's presidency during a campaign speech on Friday. "You know, if you're in doubt about somebody's name from the Middle East, just say 'Mohammad,'" Trump told a crowd in Dalton, Georgia. "You have about a 65% chance. 'Hello, Mohammad.' I've done it for years now. I've never been wrong." Mohammad is [USN:L5N3N60N8 TEXT:"one of the most common male names"] among Muslims, who often name their sons after the Prophet Mohammad, the founder of Islam. Trump made the comment as he was discussing Iran during a rally in a hangar at Dalton Municipal Airport in Georgia, where he campaigned for Republican political candidates ahead of the November 3 [TOPIC:"reuters:/world/us/elections/" TEXT:"midterm elections"]. "Iran is the only country where nobody wants to be president," Trump said, then pretended to ask several people named Mohammad whether they wanted the job. Masoud Pezeshkian has been president of Iran since 2024. The Georgia crowd gave the joke a muted response. Rights advocates and Muslim advocacy groups have repeatedly criticized Trump for rhetoric that they say demonizes and mocks Muslims, immigrants and ethnic minorities. He has [USN:L1N45U12W TEXT:"escalated"] such rhetoric during the midterm campaign season, particularly against Somali and Muslim Americans including Muslim Democratic US Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed and Representative Ilhan Omar, a Minnesota Democrat who came to the US as a Somali refugee. Trump repeated his vow that Iran would never get a nuclear weapon, seven months after the United States and Israel launched a war on Tehran aimed in part at crippling its nuclear program. An annual report by the Council on American Islamic Relations released earlier this year [USN:L4N3ZU0AN TEXT:"attributed"] rising Islamophobia in the US in part to Trump's crackdown on immigration and pro-Palestinian protests during his second term.

item.title: Professora lutou contra atirador de escola em Oregon
item.description: Uma professora da escola em Oregon onde um atirador abriu fogo e matou três crianças e um adulto jogou seu celular no agressor, o derrubou e lutou com ele em um ato que salvou vidas, informou a polícia nesta sexta-feira.
item.dc:creator: Herbert Villarraga, Deborah Bloom
item.content:encoded: Uma professora da escola em Oregon onde um atirador abriu fogo e matou três crianças e um adulto jogou seu celular no agressor, o derrubou e lutou com ele em um ato que salvou vidas, informou a polícia nesta sexta-feira. Um dia após o início da investigação sobre o mais recente tiroteio em escola nos EUA, as autoridades divulgaram novos detalhes da cena dentro de uma sala de aula para alunos com necessidades especiais da Escola Primária Silver Rail, onde três crianças de 5, 8 e 11 anos e um adulto foram mortos por um ex-aluno de 16 anos. O chefe de polícia de Bend, Mike Krantz, não identificou a professora que lutou contra o agressor, mas disse em uma coletiva de imprensa que ela jogou seu celular no suspeito, o derrubou e lutou para tirar a espingarda dele. “Ela não ficou ferida nesse incidente, mas quase certamente ajudou a impedir mais derramamento de sangue”, disse Krantz. Enquanto os dois lutavam, um pai entrou na sala de aula e abriu fogo contra o atirador, matando-o. Autoridades informaram que o pai havia seguido o atirador até dentro da escola, após testemunhá-lo disparando uma espingarda do lado de fora do campus. Quando a polícia chegou, três minutos após receber a primeira chamada, o atirador já estava morto, informou a polícia. Antes disso, o agressor de 16 anos, que havia atirado através de portas de vidro trancadas para entrar na escola, havia matado quatro pessoas e ferido outras duas. Ao se referir ao heroísmo demonstrado pela professora que se jogou sobre o suspeito e pelo pai que atirou nele, Krantz disse: “Não acho que possamos subestimar ou menosprezar essa coragem. Quando alguém está disposto a arriscar a própria vida pelos outros, nós reconhecemos isso”. Ele disse que as ações das pessoas que estavam por perto “sem dúvida salvaram vidas” e que “a professora que se dispôs a enfrentar e lutar por seus alunos, isso é verdadeiro heroísmo”. Krantz identificou o atirador como Griffin J. John 2º, que estava armado com uma espingarda calibre 12. Ele disparou cerca de 15 tiros na sala de aula e tinha mais 44 cartuchos consigo. O pai que matou o atirador foi identificado como Kaylub Giamanco, segundo o New York Times. A mãe dele o identificou, relatando que ele é pai de duas meninas que estudam na escola, de acordo com um vídeo publicado pelo New York Times. Moradores de Bend, cidade com cerca de 100 mil habitantes a cerca de 280 km a sudeste de Portland, se reuniram perto da escola para prestar homenagem na manhã desta sexta-feira, colocando flores e velas perto da fita amarela de isolamento que cercava o local do crime. Brooke Olsen, mãe de uma aluna do jardim de infância que se reuniu em segurança com sua família após o tiroteio, também expressou gratidão ao homem que deteve o atirador. “Este é um dia extremamente doloroso e de luto para todos em Bend, especialmente para as famílias da Silver Rail, e precisamos pensar no que vem a seguir em termos de medidas de segurança.” Ataques a tiros em escolas tornaram-se comuns nos EUA, e cada um deles reacende os debates sobre as leis de porte de armas em um país onde o direito de “possuir e portar armas” é protegido pela Segunda Emenda da Constituição. Alguns dos ataques mais mortíferos em escolas nos EUA incluem os ocorridos na Columbine High School em 1999, na Sandy Hook Elementary School em 2012, na Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School em 2018 e na Robb Elementary School em Uvalde, Texas, em 2022.

item.title: Lula vai enviar na próxima semana PEC que zera tarifa do transporte coletivo
item.description: O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva deve enviar já na próxima semana -- a última antes da realização do segundo turno da eleição presidencial -- a Proposta de Emenda à Constituição (PEC) que garante transporte público urbano gratuito nos finais de semana em todo o país, afirmou nesta sexta-feira o coordenador político da campanha do petista, senador Camilo Santana (PT-CE).
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva deve enviar já na próxima semana -- a última antes da realização do segundo turno da eleição presidencial -- a Proposta de Emenda à Constituição (PEC) que garante transporte público urbano gratuito nos finais de semana em todo o país, afirmou nesta sexta-feira o coordenador político da campanha do petista, senador Camilo Santana (PT-CE). A ideia, explicou Santana, é utilizar parte da verba destinada a emendas parlamentares para custear as tarifas zero de transporte. "A PEC está pronta e provavelmente o presidente deve encaminhar ao Congresso Nacional na semana que vem", disse a jornalistas. "Claro que a PEC será debatida com os congressistas, onde ele propõe exatamente como o trabalhador vai ter dois dias de descanso, ele possa ter os dois dias do final de semana com transporte gratuito para levar os seus filhos, seus familiares, com lazer, com passeio nesse país onde tiver transporte público", afirmou. O Congresso Nacional aprovou e promulgou nesta semana outra PEC, que põe fim à escala de trabalho 6x1 no Brasil, prevendo novo regime com duas folgas semanais, sendo que uma delas caia preferencialmente no domingo.

item.title: Anthropic signs lease for first Canadian data center
item.description: Anthropic has signed a lease with EverWind for data center capacity at Point Tupper, Nova Scotia, marking the Claude maker’s first data center agreement in Canada, a company executive said on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Anthropic has signed a lease with EverWind for data center capacity at Point Tupper, Nova Scotia, marking the Claude maker’s first data center agreement in Canada, a company executive said on Friday. Here are some more details: Separately, EverWind unveiled plans to invest more than C$10 billion in the data center campus and wind power projects in Nova Scotia, calling it the largest privately funded investment in the province’s history. Data centers have faced criticism over their heavy power and water use and the strain they place on local infrastructure. Jacob Glick, Anthropic’s head of public policy for Canada, said the company would protect ratepayers and water resources while ensuring local communities benefit. Anthropic [USN:L4N4500J8 TEXT:"spent"] $7.33 billion on computing and infrastructure last year, a threefold surge from 2024. The company is preparing for a US IPO that could value it at more than $2 trillion, although New York City Comptroller Mark Levine has [USN:L4N46113W TEXT:"urged"] it to delay the offering over safety and governance concerns.

item.title: Connor Bedard, Blackhawks eye third straight home win vs. Stars
item.description: The Chicago Blackhawks are playing with confidence now that Connor Bedard has returned to the ice.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The Chicago Blackhawks are playing with confidence now that Connor Bedard has returned to the ice. Looking to remain undefeated with their fourth-year star in the lineup this season, the Blackhawks also aim to continue their recent home success against the Dallas Stars on Saturday night. Chicago won once in its first six games before its young captain returned from shoulder surgery Tuesday, helping the Blackhawks to a 5-3 victory over Pittsburgh. He recorded an assist in the contest, then added another helper and scored his first goal of the season during Chicago's 4-3 overtime triumph over Winnipeg on Thursday. "We are building on how we want to play, on that identity on how we want to play," Blackhawks coach Jeff Blashill told Chicago Sports Network. Coming off his first 30-goal season, which also produced a career-best 75 points, Bedard has helped the club reset its season this week. He is joined by Blackhawks legend Patrick Kane, who has posted four points in the last four contests. "They've done a real good job of playing off each other," Blashill added. "Kaner is one of the best to ever play. Connor is making his way towards that. He is an elite, elite player in this league." With two assists Thursday, Kane became the all-time leader among American-born players with 895 assists. "We got a little bit of momentum," Kane said. "We want to keep it going." Kane has 77 points in 68 career games against Dallas, while Bedard has recorded five goals and two assists in eight career contests against the Stars. Dallas has won 14 of the last 19 meetings with the Blackhawks. However, three of Chicago's victories came in the last four meetings at the United Center. The Blackhawks have totaled 14 goals and gone 5-for-12 on the power play during their last four home games against Dallas. After dropping their first two games of the season, the Stars are 3-1-1 and recently split a home-and-home series with rival Colorado. After falling 3-2 at home to the Avalanche on Tuesday, Dallas earned a shootout victory by the same score one night later in Denver. "These (close, competitive) games are going to help us moving forward, because they springboard us into a different quadrant of play," Stars coach Glen Gulutzan said. The Stars are 2-1-1 on the road this season. Dallas forward Mikko Rantanen, who recorded an assist Wednesday, has posted six of his team-leading seven points away from home. Rantanen scored in each of his last three games against Chicago and has totaled 39 points in 30 career games against the Blackhawks. Teammate Miro Heiskanen has tallied four of his six points this season over the last three contests. Dallas goaltenders Jake Oettinger (five starts) and Casey DeSmith (two starts) have combined for a 1.71 goals-against average this season. Meanwhile, the Blackhawks are 3-1-0 at home with Spencer Knight in net. He has recorded at least 31 saves in two of those contests. Chicago backup Arvid Soderblom, however, has allowed nine goals on 50 shots in his two starts this season, both on the road. --Field Level Media

item.title: US air traffic controllers to get 2.8% pay raise under FAA deal
item.description: Thousands of US air traffic controllers will get a 2.8% pay raise retroactive to January 1 under a deal announced by the Federal Aviation Administration and a union.
item.dc:creator: David Shepardson, Doyinsola Oladipo
item.content:encoded: Thousands of US air traffic controllers will get a 2.8% pay raise retroactive to January 1 under a deal announced by the Federal Aviation Administration and a union. The pay raise, which was authorized by Congress, will be effective October 18 Controllers previously received a 1% raise but the remainder of the $140 million raise was contingent on workforce reforms The agreed changes include tracking of controllers' time, aligning staffing with demand, and improving controller reassignments The FAA has been working to address a persistent shortage of air traffic controllers Many are working mandatory overtime and six-day weeks Local managers and union representatives will now develop shift guidelines based on anticipated workload and operational requirements to ensure more productive controller schedules that maximize coverage during peak traffic hours

item.title: Wings seek home-ice turnaround as Sharks continue road trip
item.description: The Detroit Red Wings began the season with an unusually heavy home schedule. The final game of that stretch comes Saturday night when they host the San Jose Sharks.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The Detroit Red Wings began the season with an unusually heavy home schedule. The final game of that stretch comes Saturday night when they host the San Jose Sharks. Detroit opened the season with four straight home games. Following its first road contest, the Red Wings returned for a three-game homestand. They haven't protected home ice particularly well, as their 2-1 victory over winless Philadelphia on Thursday was only their second home win. Defenseman Anton Johansson had a memorable night, scoring his first NHL goal. "It was awesome (to get the win), that was the most important thing," Johansson said. "We've been struggling a little bit with the wins, but I feel we've been playing all right. It's finally nice to get it done." Center Andrew Copp, who contributed just one assist during the first six games, scored the game-winner in the third period. "You're not going to get Grade A chances night after night -- this league is too tight-checking -- but they have to start going in at some point," Copp said. "I've had some good chances and missed my spot by a couple of inches here or there. Then you're kind of fighting it or gripping the stick, so it's good to see one go in, and hopefully we can keep it going." With a four-game road trip looming, the Red Wings could use another win to build momentum. Detroit entered Thursday's game on a three-game skid, including losses in a shootout and overtime. "Even in the three losses, other than Seattle (6-3 defeat), we didn't give up a lot and played pretty decent games," Copp said. "There's just that extra two percent, like in my case not finishing, or getting pucks out or an extra battle at the end. The margin of error is so small in this league anyway, and we're not scoring six goals a night, so it might be even smaller for us." San Jose has a 4-3 record despite living on the edge. All four of its victories have come in overtime or shootouts, including a 3-2 shootout win at Nashville on Thursday. The Sharks appeared headed for their first regulation victory until the Predators' Steven Stamkos scored with one second remaining. San Jose goalie Alex Nedeljkovic, who played two seasons with Detroit, stopped 32 shots and didn't allow a goal against three skaters in the shootout. "He was unbelievable," forward Will Smith said. "He won that game for us. He was unbelievable all night. You always feel comfortable with him back there." San Jose had lost three of its previous four contests. "For the most part, I liked a lot of our game," coach Ryan Warsofsky said. "I thought there was some improvement in some areas. There are still areas to work on, but we'll take the two points and move on." The Sharks will be playing the second game of a six-game road trip Saturday. The Red Wings swept the two-game series last season. --Field Level Media

item.title: Principal órgão mundial de ciência climática suspende reunião sem chegar a acordo sobre cronograma de importante revisão
item.description: Uma reunião dos membros do Painel Intergovernamental sobre Mudanças Climáticas (IPCC) foi suspensa sem que se chegasse a um acordo sobre um cronograma para a publicação de sua próxima revisão das descobertas científicas mais recentes sobre o aquecimento global, informou o IPCC nesta sexta-feira.
item.dc:creator: Sudarshan Varadhan
item.content:encoded: Uma reunião dos membros do Painel Intergovernamental sobre Mudanças Climáticas (IPCC) foi suspensa sem que se chegasse a um acordo sobre um cronograma para a publicação de sua próxima revisão das descobertas científicas mais recentes sobre o aquecimento global, informou o IPCC nesta sexta-feira. O impasse sobre o cronograma, que já dura quase três anos, pode levar os países a decidirem a próxima fase das ações climáticas sem consenso sobre questões críticas, incluindo até que ponto parte do aquecimento global poderia ser reversível. A reunião foi suspensa depois que ultrapassou a duração prevista no último dia e muitas delegações de países menos desenvolvidos e pequenos Estados insulares tiveram que partir, informou o IPCC em um comunicado. Chegar a um acordo sobre as datas de publicação de sua próxima revisão das evidências científicas mais recentes era o principal item da pauta da reunião do IPCC com 195 Estados-membros, realizada nesta semana na capital etíope, Adis Abeba. Os governos devem avaliar o progresso em direção às metas estabelecidas no Acordo de Paris de 2015 nas negociações climáticas da ONU em novembro de 2028, no chamado “Balanço Global”. As discussões sobre o cronograma da revisão e o orçamento do IPCC “permanecem em aberto”, e as deliberações do painel serão retomadas assim que possível, informou o IPCC, sem fornecer detalhes. A possibilidade de os relatórios do IPCC não estarem prontos a tempo para as negociações climáticas de 2028 tem alarmado uma coalizão de 30 países, incluindo nações europeias, latino-americanas e pequenos Estados insulares que pressionam por ações imediatas. No entanto, países como Índia, Quênia, Arábia Saudita, Rússia e China estão pressionando por mais tempo para preparar os próximos relatórios do IPCC, a fim de garantir que cientistas de países com menos recursos possam dar contribuições significativas. “Estávamos aqui para trabalhar, mas vimos todas as propostas serem rejeitadas — sobre inclusão, sobre a relevância da ciência para nosso planejamento nacional, sobre a necessidade de evidências para orientar o próximo Balanço Global”, disse Tina Stege, enviada climática das Ilhas Marshall. “O progresso foi bloqueado até o fim — uma manobra vergonhosa para ganhar tempo quando não há tempo a perder.” As análises do IPCC têm grande peso, pois são elaboradas por centenas de especialistas internacionais e aprovadas por todos os Estados-membros, além de serem utilizadas pelos governos para planejar respostas às mudanças climáticas e citadas em decisões de tribunais internacionais. O Programa das Nações Unidas para o Meio Ambiente tem afirmado repetidamente que os esforços globais para limitar o aquecimento estão aquém do necessário e que são necessárias reduções mais profundas nas emissões para evitar desastres relacionados ao clima.

item.title: Anthropic quietly pitches its own AI safety bill to lawmakers, Politico reports
item.description: Anthropic representatives have quietly pitched Capitol Hill lawmakers on a draft bill to regulate frontier AI safety and security, Politico reported on Friday, citing three people with knowledge of the efforts.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Anthropic representatives have quietly pitched Capitol Hill lawmakers on a draft bill to regulate frontier AI safety and security, Politico reported on Friday, citing three people with knowledge of the efforts. The bill would let the government block a model's release or use only if it poses a foreseeable, imminent risk of more than $1 billion in damages, or of killing or seriously injuring more than 50 people, according to the report. Here are some details: The risk must stem from the creation or release of a biological weapon, the model evading its developer’s controls or a cyberattack, Politico reported An Anthropic spokesperson told Reuters the bill represents proposals outlined in Anthropic's "Advanced AI Framework " released earlier this year The bill would grant the government the "ability to block or deter dangerous deployments of the most powerful models," and also requires developers to test frontier AI models, be transparent about findings, and get them independently evaluated, the spokesperson said The Department of Commerce did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment Under the bill, independent evaluators, which would register with the Commerce Department, would be tasked with periodically evaluating the lab and its frontier models, according to the report The labs could pay these evaluators, provided the payment is not tied to the evaluation's outcome, the report said If the evaluators determine there is “imminent enumerated risk” for a company’s frontier models, they must report it to Commerce within 72 hours of completing their assessment, Politico reported While the Commerce Department could request a judge to halt a model after determining risk, the language explicitly prohibits any other US government department, agency, or officer from suspending development, deployment, or internal use, according to the report A federal judge for the District Court for the District of Columbia could order the suspension of a model, the report said

item.title: Eagles move RB Will Shipley to IR; Saquon Barkley out vs. Panthers
item.description: The Philadelphia Eagles' running back woes continued Friday as the team placed Will Shipley, who started last week, on injured reserve with a foot injury.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Philadelphia Eagles' running back woes continued Friday as the team placed Will Shipley, who started last week, on injured reserve with a foot injury. Shipley reportedly suffered a partial tear of his plantar fascia during the first half of Philadelphia's 19-17 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars in London last Sunday. Shipley was making just his second career start because Saquon Barkley (hamstring) was sidelined and backup Tank Bigsby (core muscle injury) had been placed on injured reserve. On Friday, Barkley was ruled out again for the Eagles' Week 6 home game against the Carolina Panthers, leaving Dameon Pierce and Carson Steele as the only healthy running backs on the active roster. Shipley, 24, had 20 carries for 57 yards and scored his first career touchdown through the first five games of this season, his third since the Eagles selected him in the fourth round of the 2024 draft. Barkley, the 2024 Offensive Player of the Year, will miss his second straight game after injuring his hamstring early in a Week 4 contest against the Los Angeles Rams. --Field Level Media

item.title: North Korea tests new AI-equipped torpedo, KCNA says
item.description: North Korea conducted an underwater test of a new torpedo weapon system on Thursday to verify technological upgrades, state news agency KCNA reported on Saturday, describing the test as a success and a significant step in the country's naval development.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: North Korea conducted an underwater test of a new torpedo weapon system on Thursday to verify technological upgrades, state news agency KCNA reported on Saturday, describing the test as a success and a significant step in the country's naval development. The test verified propulsion technology developed through more than 180 tests over the past five years, KCNA said, adding that artificial intelligence was used for target detection and guidance in the new high-speed precision-guided torpedo. The test is the latest in a run of North Korean weapons launches. It comes amid heightened tensions on the Korean Peninsula, as both Koreas race to develop weapons capable of evading missile defences. The test was part of routine defence research activities aimed at advancing the country's weapons systems, KCNA said, adding that it demonstrated improvements in propulsion efficiency and the performance of the torpedo's rocket propulsion system. The latest test came after North Korea said it had tested two types of [USN:L1N46015Q TEXT:"submarine-launched strategic cruise missiles"] on Wednesday to verify its navy's mission capabilities and the reliability of its war deterrent. Pyongyang has been seeking to develop modern missile submarines alongside ballistic and cruise missiles, test-launching them from various platforms, including an aging submarine. Meanwhile, South Korean President Lee Jae Myung oversaw the country's first test-firing of a [USN:L1N45U08H TEXT:"domestically developed hypersonic missile"] last week. Seoul's test of a hypersonic glide vehicle, a maneuverable weapon that can change course during flight, came days after North Korea said its leader, [USN:L1N45P05R TEXT:"Kim Jong Un"], had also overseen a test of an intermediate-range hypersonic missile.

item.title: Moldova condemns Russia after five drones crash on its territory
item.description: Moldova condemned Russia on Friday after five drones identified by its authorities as Russian crashed in the country in less than 24 hours.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Moldova condemned Russia on Friday after five drones identified by its authorities as Russian crashed in the country in less than 24 hours. Moldova's pro-European government, which hopes to join the European Union by 2030, has denounced Russia's invasion of Ukraine and repeatedly criticised the incursions into its airspace. Moldova shares a border with Ukraine. One drone last week crashed about 35 km (21 miles) from the capital Chisinau. The five drones entered Moldovan airspace over a little more than 17 hours on Thursday and Friday. All of them crashed, mainly in the northern and eastern districts, lightly injuring one person and causing minor damage. "These incidents pose a threat to citizens' safety and show the direct consequences for regional stability of Russia's aggressive war against Ukraine," the foreign ministry said in a statement. The incidents have repeatedly prompted the ministry to summon Russian ambassador Oleg Ozerov to demand explanations. President Maia Sandu regularly criticises Russian foreign policy as running counter to Moldova's interests and has declined to allow Ozerov to present his credentials although he has been stationed in Moldova for more than two years. Russia accuses Sandu of pursuing policies hostile to Russia. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said on Thursday that any improvement of ties with Moldova was possible only if Sandu's government "abandoned its policies based on Russophobia."

item.title: Actor Selma Blair did not intend harm on flight, spokesperson says
item.description: A representative for Selma Blair, who was arrested this week and charged with assault for actions on a US Delta Air Lines flight, said on Friday the actor did not intend to harm anyone or open an aircraft door.
item.dc:creator: Danielle Broadway, Lisa Richwine
item.content:encoded: A representative for Selma Blair, who was [USN:L6N45Y14S TEXT:"arrested this week and charged with assault"] for actions on a US Delta Air Lines flight, said on Friday the actor did not intend to harm anyone or open an aircraft door. A statement issued by her publicist repeated comments from earlier this week that Blair, who has multiple sclerosis, suffered a medical emergency on the flight from Los Angeles to New York. Blair did not try to open a door on the plane as some media outlets reported, the statement said. "There was no attempt to open the door of the aircraft. Selma did not intend to harm anyone," the statement said. Blair pleaded not guilty on Monday to charges of assaulting a police officer involved in her arrest at New York's John F. Kennedy Airport and a nurse at the hospital where she was taken afterward. Police met the plane when it landed after reports of a "physically abusive passenger" who was identified as Blair, according to a statement from the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey's police department. Two flight attendants reported injuries and one of them was taken to a hospital, police said. Blair, 54, is known for roles in "Cruel Intentions" and "Hellboy." She has spoken publicly about being diagnosed with multiple sclerosis in 2018. The statement by Blair's representative said Blair has a neurological condition known as pseudobulbar affect, "which bears directly on how a medical episode presents to people who do not know her." "There is much more to this story than has been reported, and we ask to consider the entirety of the facts before rushing to judgment, whether in the courtroom or in the court of public opinion," Blair's representatives said.

item.title: Forças russas tomam Dobropillia, no leste da Ucrânia, diz ministro, mas não há confirmação de Kiev
item.description: O ministro da Defesa da Rússia, Andrei Belousov, afirmou nesta sexta-feira que as forças de Moscou haviam capturado a cidade de Dobropillia, na região de Donetsk, no leste da Ucrânia.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O ministro da Defesa da Rússia, Andrei Belousov, afirmou nesta sexta-feira que as forças de Moscou haviam capturado a cidade de Dobropillia, na região de Donetsk, no leste da Ucrânia. A Ucrânia não fez menção à mudança de controle de Dobropillia. A cidade, localizada a sudoeste dos importantes centros de Kramatorsk e Sloviansk, vem sofrendo ataques russos contínuos há algum tempo. As Forças Armadas ucranianas informaram nesta sexta-feira que as forças russas estavam tentando avançar nas proximidades de Dobropillia, e o presidente ucraniano, Volodymyr Zelenskiy, afirmou no início desta semana que as tropas russas estavam sofrendo baixas nos arredores da cidade. Belousov também disse que as forças de Moscou haviam capturado dois vilarejos no leste da Ucrânia: Oleksiievo-Druzhkivka, na mesma área da região de Donetsk, e Velykomykhaylivka, na região de Dnipropetrovsk. As forças russas vêm avançando lentamente pela região de Donetsk e por outras partes do leste da Ucrânia, embora o ritmo de seus avanços tenha diminuído nos últimos meses.

item.title: WNBA: Experts anticipate defensive showdown in Dream v Valkyries Finals
item.description: Fans can expect a clash of two defensive powerhouses when the WNBA Finals kick off on Saturday between the Dream and the Golden State Valkyries, with Angel Reese ready to deliver after a career-best season for Atlanta.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Fans can expect a clash of two defensive powerhouses when the WNBA Finals kick off on Saturday between the Dream and the Golden State Valkyries, with Angel Reese ready to deliver after a career-best season for Atlanta. The two sides accounted for six of the WNBA's 10 All-Defensive first and second teams this season, with the showdown centering largely on "who stays healthy defensively", Hall of Famer Tamika Catchings told reporters this week. "They're so similar as far as player for player and what they bring," said Catchings, a USA Sports analyst. The Dream scored big when they snared WNBA defensive player of the year Reese from Chicago this season, as the "Bayou Barbie" brought buzz and a brick wall to Atlanta with 12.1 rebounds averaged per game, while their late-season acquisition of six-time All-Star DeWanna Bonner ensured their first trip to the finals in 13 years. WAIT AND SEE FOR GRAY The biggest question mark hanging over the Dream is the status of their leading scorer Allisha Gray, who injured her shooting hand during the semi-final series against New York. She reportedly underwent a minor surgical procedure during the week-long downtime between the penultimate stage and the finals, and is questionable to play in Game 1 against Golden State. "The reason I give maybe a slight, slight razor’s edge to Atlanta is only because of the scoring power that they have," said Hall of Famer and NBC commentator Cheryl Miller. "Now with possibly seeing... Allisha Gray, where she may be at, that may have dissipated, so it’s just a wait-and-see." For Golden State, the Finals represent a chance of extending a remarkable run from 2025 league debutant to WNBA powerhouse, with 2025 WNBA Coach of the Year Natalie Nakase providing the blueprint for future expansion teams coming behind them. The Valkyries were the first expansion team in league history to make the playoffs a year ago and, with French All-Star Gabby Williams (14.4 points 3.3 rebounds 1.6 steals) at the helm and center Kiah Stokes joining from the Las Vegas Aces this season, they became the first to reach the Finals in their second year. "It's going to be a low-scoring game, all of them. I think it's going to be a huge battle, but when I look at Kiah Stokes specifically, I'd say she's probably one of - when we talk about her in general, one of the more undervalued players," said Catchings. Game 1 of the best-of-seven series is on Saturday in San Francisco.

item.title: Missiles hit Aden airport as Saudi-led coalition intercepts missile headed for Yanbu
item.description: Missiles struck Yemen's Aden International Airport on Friday, while a Saudi-led military coalition said it had intercepted a ballistic missile headed for the Red Sea city of Yanbu, a key Saudi oil hub that allows exports to avoid the Strait of Hormuz.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Missiles struck Yemen's Aden International Airport on Friday, while a Saudi-led military coalition said it had intercepted a ballistic missile headed for the Red Sea city of Yanbu, a key Saudi oil hub that allows exports to avoid the Strait of Hormuz. The coalition said it had also destroyed two cruise missiles over the Red Sea and three drones in Saudi Arabia's Southern and Riyadh regions. It did not identify the attackers. In Aden in southern Yemen, two missiles landed on the airport grounds, the Aden Security Department said, blaming the Iran-aligned Houthi group. It said the incident was the second attack on the facility in less than a week. The Houthis did not immediately claim responsibility. No casualties were reported. A Yemenia Airways flight bound for Cairo was preparing for takeoff when the missiles landed, the security department said. Yanbu is a key outlet for Saudi oil exports, allowing the kingdom to ship crude to international markets via the Red Sea, bypassing the Strait of Hormuz. The vital waterway has been largely throttled by Iran since the US and Israel launched attacks on the country in February. With regional tensions and security threats raising concerns over the safety of shipping and tighter global energy supplies, Brent crude oil briefly touched [USN:L1N46201B TEXT:"$110 a barrel"] on Friday for the first time since May. Saudi Civil Defense authorities issued an alert early on Saturday for Abha in southwestern Saudi Arabia near the Yemeni border before sending an all-clear. Earlier they had issued alerts in the Jazan region and the southwestern city of Khamis Mushait, where such warnings have become frequent since fighting resumed last month. Also early on Saturday, Houthi-affiliated media reported strikes east of Yemen's northwestern city of Saada. The Saudi-led coalition said it had destroyed two ballistic missile launchers in the area. Fighting between the Houthis and a Saudi-led coalition backing Yemen's government has raised fears of a further deterioration in the country's humanitarian crisis. Aid agencies have warned that conditions are worsening rapidly. The Yemen conflict has become another front as the Iran war has widened into a regional conflict. The Houthis seized the capital Sanaa in 2014 and forced the internationally recognised government south. A Saudi-led intervention began the following year, leading to years of stalemate before a 2022 truce that held until this year. The Houthis have repeatedly launched missiles and drones at Saudi Arabia since the conflict reignited, [USN:L1N4610QE TEXT:"targeting"] [USN:L1N45W03M TEXT:"airports,"] oil facilities and other infrastructure. In recent days, the group has also targeted sites in government-held parts of Yemen, including Aden airport and the presidential palace in the interim capital. A spokesperson for the Houthi-run health ministry said on Friday that 124 civilians had been killed and 327 wounded in what he described as "Saudi aggression" since the escalation began on September 3. Reuters could not independently verify the figures.

item.title: US lifts curbs on Mexican airlines after aviation dispute
item.description: Mexican airlines will be able to launch new flights to the US from Mexico City's two international airports after the US Department of Transportation lifted restrictions imposed over aviation disputes between the two countries, Mexico's government said on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Mexican airlines will be able to launch new flights to the US from Mexico City's two international airports after the US Department of Transportation lifted restrictions imposed over aviation disputes between the two countries, Mexico's government said on Friday. The decision allows airlines to establish routes to the US from Mexico City's Felipe Angeles International Airport (AIFA) and Benito Juarez International Airport, according to a statement from the ministries of foreign affairs and communications and transportation. The US Department of Transportation said the move reflected steps taken by Mexico to address concerns over its compliance with a 2015 bilateral air transport agreement. The department said it would continue to require Mexican carriers to file schedules for flights to and from the US and obtain approval to operate services using large aircraft. A US official said two other orders related to the dispute remain in place and that Washington would closely monitor Mexico's compliance with its commitments. The official said the decision was separate from an ongoing Federal Aviation Administration review of Mexico's aviation oversight efforts conducted in August. The FAA restored Mexico's top air safety rating in September 2023, allowing Mexican airlines to expand existing US routes and launch new services. Mexico had been downgraded in May 2021 after the US regulator found the country did not meet international aviation safety standards. The downgrade was a major blow to [USN:L1N38K2PD TEXT:"Mexican carriers"], as US airlines were able to scoop up market share. In May , US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said the Mexican government had agreed to improve aviation access to Mexico City. President Donald Trump's administration had reached an agreement with Mexico on a plan to address US concerns over its compliance with a 2015 air transport agreement between the two countries, Duffy said. [USN:L1N3W91NS TEXT:"In October"] last year, the US froze the expansion of Mexican airlines' passenger and cargo services from the two airports, alleging Mexico had not complied with the bilateral aviation agreement since 2022, when it rescinded slots held by US passenger airlines and forced US all-cargo carriers to relocate operations. Mexican airlines welcomed Friday's decision. Carriers Viva and Aeromexico (AERO.MX) said it would strengthen air connectivity between the two countries.

item.title: Trump administration loses bid to disqualify Susman Godfrey from lawyer group's lawsuit
item.description: A US judge on Friday allowed law firm Susman Godfrey to continue representing the American Bar Association in its lawsuit against President Donald Trump's administration, rejecting government arguments that the firm's involvement in matters at issue in the litigation created a conflict requiring its disqualification.
item.dc:creator: Mike Scarcella
item.content:encoded: A US judge on Friday allowed law firm Susman Godfrey to continue representing the American Bar Association in its lawsuit against President Donald Trump's administration, rejecting government arguments that the firm's involvement in matters at issue in the litigation created a conflict requiring its disqualification. US District Judge Amir Ali in Washington wrote in his ruling that the Trump administration had not shown that lawyers at Susman Godfrey would simultaneously appear as witnesses in the lawsuit while also representing the ABA. Even if there were such a witness, professional attorney rules would not automatically disqualify the rest of the law firm, wrote Ali, an appointee of Democratic President Joe Biden. "That the ABA seeks discovery about communications related to Susman Godfrey does not indicate the lawyers representing the ABA here, who may not have even been involved in the communications, are likely to be necessary witnesses," Ali wrote. The White House had no immediate comment. The American Bar Association did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The [USN:L6N4001DA TEXT:"ABA filed the lawsuit last year"], alleging the Trump administration adopted an unlawful policy of targeting law firms and lawyers based on their legal work, hiring, diversity policies and political ties. Susman Godfrey was among Trump's targets in a series of executive orders targeting law firms . It is one of three law firms that won court orders last year permanently barring enforcement of the orders against them. The Trump administration's [USN:L6N41Q0B7 TEXT:"appeal"] is pending. The Trump administration in July [USN:L6N43M061 TEXT:"asked Ali to disqualify"] Susman Godfrey from representing the American Bar Association. The administration said that removing Susman would not harm the ABA, because the organization "may have as its choice of counsel presumably any law firm in the country, or at least most law firms." The ABA and Susman Godfrey opposed the government’s disqualification effort. They assailed the administration’s bid as "a new chapter in the ongoing effort to intimidate and chill the speech of the American legal profession." The case is American Bar Association v. Executive Office of the President, US District Court for the District of Columbia, No. 1:25-cv-01888-AHA. item.title: Grynspan holds lead for next UN chief as race enters decisive stage
item.description: An informal poll by the United Nations Security Council on Friday placed former Costa Rican Vice President Rebeca Grynspan as the narrow frontrunner in the race to become the 10th UN secretary-general, two people close to the process said.
item.dc:creator: Antoni Slodkowski
item.content:encoded: An informal poll by the United Nations Security Council on Friday placed former Costa Rican Vice President Rebeca Grynspan as the narrow frontrunner in the race to become the 10th UN secretary-general, two people close to the process said. But there was no clear winner as all candidates received two or more opposing votes from the ultimately decisive five permanent members of the council — Russia, China, the US, France and Britain — opening the door for new candidates to join the race, diplomats and observers said. [USN:L8N41304B TEXT:"Whoever wins"] will have to tackle multiple crises, including several wars, cutbacks in American contributions to the UN, and the 193-member body's declining political relevance as Washington has pulled out of dozens of its agencies. This was the [USN:L6N3W20WS TEXT:"sixth secret ballot"] organized by council officials, who have less than three months to pick the successor to UN chief Antonio Guterres, whose term ends on December 31. Securing the council's recommendation requires at least nine positive votes of the 15 countries and no "discourage" votes from the five permanent members. The race has entered a decisive stage, as Friday's poll for the first time used color-coded ballots revealing whether a veto power opposes a candidate. Four of five polls in recent months showed Grynspan, 70, narrowly ahead, with one poll in August placing Guyana's UN ambassador Carolyn Rodrigues-Birkett in the top spot. This dynamic did not fundamentally change on Friday, with Grynspan receiving nine "encourage," five "discourage" and one "no opinion" vote, with two of the five opposing votes coming from the Security Council's permanent members, people close to the process said. Rodrigues-Birkett received eight votes in favor, six against, and one "no opinion," with two opposing votes from the permanent members. Rafael Grossi, director general of the UN nuclear watchdog, received a near-identical result to Rodrigues-Birkett, but with one fewer permanent member supporting his bid. Four more former UN officials and senior diplomats are vying for support, but they have received more opposing than supporting votes, indicating waning enthusiasm for their candidacies. Diplomats say several senior figures, including former and current foreign ministers and country leaders, are considering entering the race. Any new entrant will face a steep challenge of convincing the divided council in short order. On the question of new contenders joining the race, Washington's envoy to the UN, Mike Waltz, said after the vote: "Countries, if they want to put more candidates in, that's certainly within their sovereign rights." When Guterres was chosen in October 2016, it took six straw polls for the council to reach agreement. In the more than 80-year history of the UN, there has never been a female secretary-general. In an [USN:L1N46112N TEXT:"interview with Reuters on Thursday"], Grynspan said she "wouldn't be surprised" to receive a veto and said that it would be just the start of negotiations as such blocking votes have been overcome by winning contenders in past races. "The game is not over -- we will have to continue working," she said. The Costa Rican economist added that the UN has become too risk-averse and its next leader must be prepared to bear the cost of diplomatic failure and try again. She also said the UN must cut top jobs, curb bureaucracy and stop agencies duplicating work, arguing that cost-cutting alone would not revive an institution struggling with shrinking resources and declining political clout.

item.title: Travel booking platform Klook Technology files to withdraw US listing
item.description: Travel booking platform Klook Technology on Friday filed to withdraw its US initial public offering plans amid market volatility.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Travel booking platform Klook Technology on Friday filed to withdraw its US initial public offering plans amid market volatility. "Given current market conditions, Klook has decided this is not the right time to proceed with an IPO," a company spokesperson told Reuters. "We will continue to evaluate the right time for a listing." IPO activity in the US market has softened in recent weeks as higher bond yields, a prolonged restrictive policy outlook and geopolitical uncertainty have made investors more cautious. Klook joins smart-ring maker [USN:L4N45L0NO TEXT:"Oura"] and nuclear services company [USN:L4N4581N0 TEXT:"Holtec"] among a growing list of companies that have [USN:L4N45V00M TEXT:"deferred"] IPO plans this year as volatile markets continue to curb investor appetite for new listings. The Hong Kong-based company [USN:L4N3WM1ED TEXT:"had filed for a US IPO in November last year"], and at the time disclosed a 24% jump in 2024 revenue to $417.1 million. Founded in 2014, Klook offers bookings for tours, attractions, transport and other travel experiences across a wide range of locations globally. It competes with global platforms such as Booking.com, TripAdvisor, China's Trip.com and South Korea's Yanolja. "Our business continues to grow, with total experiences booked on track to exceed 80 million this year, the spokesperson said. Klook was aiming to list its shares on NYSE under the symbol "KLK".

item.title: Grynspan sigue a la cabeza en carrera por secretaría general ONU, que entra en una fase decisiva
item.description: Una votación informal celebrada el viernes en el Consejo de Seguridad de las Naciones Unidas situó a la exvicepresidenta de Costa Rica Rebeca Grynspan como líder por estrecho margen en la carrera por el cargo de secretario general de la ONU, afirmaron dos personas cercanas al proceso.
item.dc:creator: Antoni Slodkowski
item.content:encoded: Una votación informal celebrada el viernes en el Consejo de Seguridad de las Naciones Unidas situó a la exvicepresidenta de Costa Rica Rebeca Grynspan como líder por estrecho margen en la carrera por el cargo de secretario general de la ONU, afirmaron dos personas cercanas al proceso. Sin embargo, no hubo un ganador claro, ya que todos los candidatos recibieron dos o más votos en contra de los cinco miembros permanentes del Consejo —Rusia, China, Estados Unidos, Francia y el Reino Unido—, que son los que tienen la última palabra, lo que abre la puerta a que nuevos aspirantes se sumen a la carrera, afirmaron diplomáticos y observadores. Esta fue la sexta votación secreta organizada por los responsables del Consejo, que disponen de menos de tres meses para elegir al sucesor del jefe de la ONU, António Guterres, cuyo mandato finaliza el 31 de diciembre. Quienquiera que gane tendrá que hacer frente a múltiples crisis, entre ellas varias guerras, los recortes en las contribuciones estadounidenses a la ONU y la menguante relevancia política del organismo de 193 miembros, dado que Washington se ha retirado de docenas de sus agencias. Para obtener la recomendación del Consejo se requieren al menos nueve votos a favor de los 15 países y que ninguno de los cinco miembros permanentes emita un voto negativo. La carrera ha entrado en una fase decisiva, ya que en la votación del viernes se utilizaron por primera vez papeletas codificadas por colores que revelaban si algún miembro con derecho a veto se oponía a un candidato. Cuatro de las cinco rondas de los últimos meses mostraron a Grynspan, de 70 años, ligeramente por delante, mientras que una en agosto situó a la embajadora de Guyana ante la ONU, Carolyn Rodrigues-Birkett, en el primer puesto. Esta dinámica no cambió de forma sustancial el viernes, ya que Grynspan recibió nueve votos a favor, cinco en contra y uno de "sin opinión". Dos de los cinco votos en contra procedían de miembros permanentes del Consejo de Seguridad, dijeron fuentes. Birkett recibió ocho votos a favor, seis en contra y uno de "sin opinión", con dos votos en contra de los miembros permanentes. El argentino Rafael Grossi, director general de la agencia nuclear de la ONU, obtuvo un resultado casi idéntico al de Birkett, pero con un miembro permanente menos que apoyara su candidatura.

item.title: Spanish club fighting Thunder over Aday Mara's contractual rights
item.description: Basket Zaragoza and the Oklahoma City Thunder are at odds over the contract status of NBA lottery pick Aday Mara's eligibility to play in the NBA.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Basket Zaragoza and the Oklahoma City Thunder are at odds over the contract status of NBA lottery pick Aday Mara's eligibility to play in the NBA. The top-level Spanish club informed FIFA, the NBA and Thunder of its claim that Mara is under contract with the team for the 2026-27 season and can't play in any other professional league without an international transfer agreement. Basket Zaragoza also said it would dispute any such request. The Thunder said the NBA cleared Mara because he participated in three full years of college basketball in the NCAA. Mara played for UCLA and then transferred to Michigan and was part of the university's national championship team in April. "Aday last played three years of NCAA college basketball and therefore, as advised by the NBA, no clearance from the Spanish team is required for him to play in the NBA," a Thunder spokesperson said Friday. Mara, a 7-foot-3 center, was a member of Basket Zaragoza from 2021-23. He was the No. 12 pick in the 2026 NBA Draft. --Field Level Media

item.title: Browns rookie WR KC Concepcion cleared to play vs. Ravens
item.description: Cleveland Browns rookie receiver KC Concepcion cleared the concussion protocol and is set to play in Sunday's game against the visiting Baltimore Ravens.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Cleveland Browns rookie receiver KC Concepcion cleared the concussion protocol and is set to play in Sunday's game against the visiting Baltimore Ravens. Concepcion took a blow to the head from New York Jets safety Minkah Fitzpatrick in the first quarter last week. He remained down on the turf for a few minutes before being helped off the field. Concepcion said Friday that he had no ill will toward Fitzpatrick. "I don't fault anybody. I know the game I signed up to play," Concepcion said. "To me, it wasn't a dirty play. It was a football play." Concepcion was a full practice participant on Friday after being limited the previous two days. Concepcion was a first-round pick (No. 24 overall) by the Browns. He had one catch for five yards before exiting the 17-12 loss to the Jets. Overall, he has 18 receptions for 149 yards. Cleveland ruled out five players on Friday: defensive tackles Kalia Davis (quadriceps) and Mike Hall Jr. (ankle), quarterback Dillon Gabriel (back), guard Teven Jenkins (back) and running back Dylan Sampson (knee). Jenkins will miss his sixth straight game. Browns leading rusher Quinshon Judkins (ankle) was one of four players listed as questionable. Judkins has 221 rushing yards but just 3.0 yards per carry. Standout defensive tackle Mason Graham (knee/ankle), defensive end Derek Barnett (ankle) and linebacker Carson Schwesinger (ankle) are also questionable. Graham, who sat out against the Jets, returned to practice Friday on a limited basis. Browns coach Todd Monken is hoping to have key performers Graham and Schwesinger against Baltimore. "They're wired the right way, they just are," Monken said of the duo. "If they can go, they're going to go. And not only the way they're wired, but also in terms of how much the team means to them. That's what ‘team' says -- when you're willing to play hurt, when you're willing to chase the ball, when you're willing to be connected on a daily basis. So those guys are wired the right way." --Field Level Media

item.title: UK finance minister says Heathrow expansion would boost growth
item.description: British finance minister John Healey said expanding Heathrow Airport would help drive growth, in a show of support for the project after his boss, Prime Minister Andy Burnham, refused to back plans for a new runway.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: British finance minister John Healey said expanding Heathrow Airport would help drive growth, in a show of support for the project after his boss, Prime Minister Andy Burnham, [USN:L8N45J04N TEXT:"refused to back"] plans for a new runway. Adding an extra runway at the busiest airport in Europe is an issue that has divided British politicians for decades. Under Burnham's predecessor, Keir Starmer, the government sought to settle the matter in 2025 by saying it should go ahead. Healey told reporters at the International Monetary Fund's annual meeting in Bangkok that the project was in line with the government's central aim of strengthening the economy. "The case for a third runway at Heathrow has always been a case for growth," he said on Friday. Three weeks ago, Burnham declined to support it and said the decision was a matter for people who live near the airport. Many [USN:L6N45Y09P TEXT:"businesses, airlines and investors"] have said the airport should expand but some local residents have objected to the noise from more planes, while the UK's [USN:L6N4580BL TEXT:"climate targets"] could be at risk from adding thousands more flights. Heathrow faces a lengthy planning process before any potential construction can begin and the airport said in September that a third runway may not open until 2039, [USN:L6N45I05T TEXT:"four years later"] than forecast in an initial plan.

item.title: Kenvue loses bid for rehearing after Tylenol autism lawsuits revived
item.description: A US appeals court said on Friday it won’t reconsider a ruling reviving hundreds of lawsuits against Tylenol maker Kenvue alleging the popular painkiller can cause autism.
item.dc:creator: Diana Jones
item.content:encoded: A US appeals court said on Friday it won’t reconsider a ruling reviving hundreds of lawsuits against Tylenol maker Kenvue alleging the popular painkiller can cause autism. In a brief order, the 2nd US Circuit Court of Appeals in Manhattan said it was rejecting a request from the company, which was spun off from Johnson & Johnson, to reconsider the three-judge panel’s ruling or to have the full court hear the case In July, the panel [USN:L6N43F0XN TEXT:"revived about 500 lawsuits"] filed by parents over claims Tylenol use during pregnancy is linked to autism and attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) in children In that ruling, the court said a district court judge improperly excluded expert testimony from three doctors supporting the parents’ claims Kenvue asked the court to reconsider the decision, saying district judges are the "true gatekeepers" who decide whether evidence is reliable enough to be admitted at trial A spokesperson for Kenvue did not immediately respond to a request for comment Friday’s ruling could pave the way for the company to appeal to the US Supreme Court The issue drew greater attention after President Donald Trump and top US health officials[USN:L2N3V90HS TEXT:" suggested a link to autism"] There is[USN:L1N3US0SS TEXT:" no firm scientific evidence"] of a link between the drug and the conditions

item.title: Packers RB Josh Jacobs, Broncos LB Jonathon Cooper taken off exempt list
item.description: The NFL notified Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs and Denver Broncos linebacker Jonathon Cooper that they will be removed from the commissioner's exempt list Monday, making them eligible to return in Week 7.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The NFL notified Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs and Denver Broncos linebacker Jonathon Cooper that they will be removed from the commissioner's exempt list Monday, making them eligible to return in Week 7. Neither player has appeared in a game this season due to separate legal troubles. The league placed both men on the exempt list Aug. 30. Both Jacobs and Cooper are now allowed to practice with their respective teams in addition to appearing in games. It is not clear if their games missed while on the exempt list will be considered "time served" or if they will be suspended by the league in the future. The NFL also emphasized in its announcements that its reviews of Jacobs and Cooper under the personal conduct policy remain ongoing. Jacobs has pleaded no contest to misdemeanor charges of battery and criminal damage to property stemming from an arrest last May outside Green Bay. His legal team reportedly reached a plea agreement with the court in which he must avoid contact with his accuser, a woman, as well as receive counseling, remain under supervision of criminal justice officials and pay restitution to the woman. Jacobs, 28, is entering his third season with the Packers after spending his first five NFL seasons with the Oakland/Las Vegas Raiders. He rushed for 929 yards and 13 touchdowns last season and 1,329 yards and 15 touchdowns in 2024. Cooper was arrested twice in June on multiple charges, including a felony charge alleging strangulation and charges of misdemeanor domestic violence and harassment. In the initial incident, he and his girlfriend were arrested on June 5 on suspicion of misdemeanor domestic violence; arrest records indicated that they were having a disagreement over allegations of infidelity. Cooper was later charged with felony second-degree assault by strangulation. He was arrested again on June 12 on charges that he violated a protection order filed against him. Cooper pleaded not guilty to his charges on Aug. 31. Last week, his trial date was moved from this November to March 2-4, 2027. Cooper, 28, started all 17 games in the 2023, 2024 and 2025 seasons for the Broncos and tallied 27 sacks across those campaigns. Jacobs will be eligible to play in the Packers' Week 7 game at the Detroit Lions. The Broncos played their Week 6 game Thursday night. Cooper will be able to return for Week 7 at the Arizona Cardinals. --Field Level Media
