item.title: Uruguay football tests electronic cards in bid to modernise refereeing
item.description: A referee raised a phone-sized electronic device to caution a player during a Uruguayan cup match this week, replacing the familiar flash of a yellow card with a digital screen in a trial aimed at modernising one of football's oldest rituals.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A referee raised a phone-sized electronic device to caution a player during a Uruguayan cup match this week, replacing the familiar flash of a yellow card with a digital screen in a trial aimed at modernising one of football's oldest rituals. Match official Eduardo Varela used the device during Nacional's Copa Uruguay match against Rentistas on Thursday, testing a system designed to simplify referees' administrative work by recording disciplinary decisions digitally. "We are looking to bring technology to the only thing in football that is still analogue," said Mauro Sacco, director of REFe, the company behind the project, in an interview with Uruguayan radio El Espectador Deportes on Friday. The idea emerged more than three years ago when Sacco and fellow director Diego de la Pena watched a match in rainy conditions and considered how referees recorded cautions by hand before transferring the information to digital systems. The new device logs match incidents with timestamps, with developers aiming to streamline the submission of official records to the Uruguayan Football Association's COMET platform. VISIBILITY CHALLENGE For Varela, the new tool was comfortable to use and its software responded quickly, although he acknowledged that it lacked the drama of the traditional gesture. "You lose a little of the magic of the quick card but I think it is something that will help us a lot, especially with the administrative side," he said. The first real-world tests have also exposed a problem: visibility. An earlier trial was abandoned because sunlight made the screen difficult to see, while spectators and television viewers struggled to distinguish some decisions during Thursday's match. "It's a project with room for improvement. It looked much better live than it did on TV. The challenge we face now is to improve it for the whole audience," De la Pena said. "The yellow card has to be yellow, the red card has to be red, and it has to be visible to people at the ground and on television." The developers are exploring changes, including LED lighting around the device, to make the colours clearer to spectators. Sacco said the brand had been registered and the hardware and software patented, with the developers based in China. The trial has drawn mixed reactions online. "We have seen all kinds of comments, positive and negative. We have even laughed at the memes," he said. "The important thing is that people are talking about it. Any innovation takes time." REFe hopes to refine the technology and eventually see it adopted by South American governing body CONMEBOL and world soccer's FIFA.

item.title: LA restaurant group used $60,000 Dodgers bet to hedge playoff risk, Kalshi says
item.description: A Los Angeles hospitality group used a $60,000 trade on Kalshi to offset revenue lost after the Los Angeles Dodgers failed to reach the World Series, according to the prediction markets platform.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A Los Angeles hospitality group used a $60,000 trade on Kalshi to offset revenue lost after the Los Angeles Dodgers failed to reach the World Series, according to the prediction markets platform. Here are more details: The group, which operates 25 bars, many of them near the Dodger Stadium, made a $60,000 trade on Kalshi if the team did not advance The position returned nearly twice the original stake, Kalshi said, helping make up for business the bars would have received from additional playoff games The trade points to a small but growing use of prediction markets by businesses seeking protection against risks that conventional financial products may not cover Kalshi platforms allow users worldwide to trade binary contracts on outcomes in politics, sports, economics and entertainment

item.title: Anac restringe regras para aviação geral em Congonhas
item.description: A Agência Nacional de Aviação Civil (Anac) decidiu endurecer regras para a alocação horários de pousos e decolagens da aviação geral no aeroporto de Congonhas, na cidade de São Paulo, informou a autarquia nesta sexta feira.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A Agência Nacional de Aviação Civil (Anac) decidiu endurecer regras para a alocação horários de pousos e decolagens da aviação geral no aeroporto de Congonhas, na cidade de São Paulo, informou a autarquia nesta sexta feira. A medida foi tomada após suspeitas de que uma empresa estaria adquirindo esses slots e depois revendendo os espaços para pousos e decolagens num mercado paralelo, afirmou a agência. A aviação geral é a voltada para operações como jatos executivos, táxi aéreo e ambulâncias aéreas. Para evitar o comércio de slots, a partir de agora os operadores de aviação geral deverão contar com um provedor de serviços de base fixa (FBO, na sigla em inglês) antes de solicitar os horários de operação. A medida já foi publicada no Diário Oficial da União. A iniciativa conta com o apoio do Departamento de Controle do Espaço Aéreo (Decea). O presidente da agência, Tiago Faierstein, disse que a Anac vai acompanhar e fiscalizar de perto, de modo a acabar com o comércio paralelo de slots. "Na prática, as novas regras também restringem as condições de utilização de Congonhas pela aviação geral, ao exigir maior planejamento e comprovação prévia da estrutura necessária para cada operação", disse Faierstein. Procurada, a Aena (AENA.MC) , responsável pela administração de Congonhas, não quis comentar da decisão da Anac.

item.title: Zelenskiy critica acordo entre EUA e Rússia sobre diesel
item.description: O presidente ucraniano Volodymyr Zelenskiy condenou, nesta sexta-feira, o acordo firmado pelo presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, com a Rússia envolvendo o diesel, classificou a posição de Moscou como uma "paródia" das negociações de paz e saudou a perspectiva de um papel maior para os aliados europeus nas conversas, a quem chamou de "verdadeiros líderes".
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O presidente ucraniano Volodymyr Zelenskiy condenou, nesta sexta-feira, o acordo firmado pelo presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, com a Rússia envolvendo o diesel, classificou a posição de Moscou como uma "paródia" das negociações de paz e saudou a perspectiva de um papel maior para os aliados europeus nas conversas, a quem chamou de "verdadeiros líderes". Zelenskiy afirmou, durante uma cúpula da União Europeia em Bruxelas, que a Rússia não deseja a paz. Vestindo uniforme militar durante uma visita a um posto de comando, o presidente russo, Vladimir Putin, disse que Moscou está estabelecendo uma “zona de segurança” dentro da Ucrânia ao longo da fronteira, medida que ele considerou inegociável em quaisquer futuras negociações com Kiev. Trump disse que nem ele nem Elon Musk são responsáveis pelo fato de a Ucrânia ter perdido, nesta semana, o acesso ao serviço de satélites Starlink, de Musk, um importante elemento de defesa contra os ataques russos. Trump afirmou ter um bom relacionamento com Zelenskiy, apesar da recente troca de farpas com o líder ucraniano. Em Bruxelas, os líderes da UE se uniram em apoio a Zelenskiy após Trump voltar a criticar a Ucrânia, chamando seus ataques a refinarias russas de “vergonha”. A UE recebe Zelenskiy em um dos momentos mais difíceis para a Ucrânia, com mísseis e drones russos chovendo sobre cidades ucranianas e temores de que os EUA possam retirar o compartilhamento de inteligência e o apoio com armas a Kiev. Zelenskiy deu poucos sinais de que iria suavizar sua postura em relação a Washington. Trump pegou Zelenskiy de surpresa no último fim de semana ao anunciar que a Ucrânia e a Rússia haviam concordado em não atacar as instalações energéticas uma da outra. Às vésperas das eleições de meio de mandato, no mês que vem, Trump responsabilizou os ataques ucranianos às refinarias russas pela elevação dos preços da energia, o que pode custar ao seu Partido Republicano suas estreitas maiorias no Senado e na Câmara dos Deputados dos EUA. A Ucrânia atacou uma refinaria de petróleo russa a sudeste de Moscou na quinta-feira, depois que Zelenskiy declarou que Kiev estava abandonando o cessar-fogo no setor energético anunciado por Trump. O acordo dos EUA com a Rússia em torno do diesel irritou a Ucrânia e seus aliados europeus. “E agora podemos ver como o dinheiro começará a fluir de volta para a Rússia por meio do acordo do diesel”, disse Zelenskiy a jornalistas. “Esse acordo sobre o diesel nunca será suficiente para compensar o impacto do Estreito de Ormuz nos mercados globais. Mas vai colocar mais dinheiro diretamente no bolso de Putin para financiar essa guerra.” O presidente francês, Emmanuel Macron, disse que o acordo “não é bom para ninguém". "Ele envia um sinal negativo. É um elemento de divisão e dúvida.”

item.title: Peso mexicano anota sexta semana de pérdidas por panorama de tasas
item.description: El peso mexicano se depreció el viernes y registró su sexta semana consecutiva de pérdidas, golpeada por persistentes preocupaciones de que se reduzca el diferencial entre las tasas de interés de México y Estados Unidos.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El peso mexicano se depreció el viernes y registró su sexta semana consecutiva de pérdidas, golpeada por persistentes preocupaciones de que se reduzca el diferencial entre las tasas de interés de México y Estados Unidos. La bolsa, en tanto, anotó su mayor ganancia semanal en más de seis meses con los inversionistas evaluando los primeros resultados corporativos del tercer trimestre en Estados Unidos. En México, se esperan los primeros resultados trimestrales relevantes a partir de la próxima semana. * La moneda local cotizaba en 18.4895 unidades por dólar en la recta final de los negocios, con una depreciación del 0.51%, revirtiendo sus [USN:L1N46204Q TEXT:"ganancias iniciales"], con lo que acumulaba un retroceso semanal de un 0.54%. * "En términos generales, parece que la presión sobre el peso llegó para quedarse", afirmó James Salazar, subdirector de análisis económico de Kapital Grupo Financiero. Salazar dijo que, si persisten la volatilidad por las tasas, junto con los riesgos asociados a la situación en Medio Oriente, las elecciones de noviembre en Estados Unidos y la revisión en curso del TMEC, el peso podría acercarse a 19 por dólar, aunque cerraría el año entre 18.20 y 18.30 unidades. * Por lo pronto en el mercado de futuros de Chicago, las apuestas a favor de la moneda mexicana repuntaron levemente, luego de cuatro semanas continuas de deterioro que las llevaron a su menor nivel desde enero de 2025. * Durante la semana, el peso llegó a debilitarse hasta [USN:L1N46000S TEXT:"18.6060 unidades"], un nivel no visto desde noviembre de 2025, ante la publicación de datos económicos en Estados Unidos, principalmente de [USN:L6N4610YR TEXT:"inflación"], y declaraciones de autoridades de la Reserva Federal. * Su presidente, [USN:L6N4620BI TEXT:"Kevin Warsh"], evitó el viernes adelantar su postura sobre el rumbo de la política monetaria, durante las reuniones anuales del FMI y el Banco Mundial en Bangkok, afianzando las expectativas de que la Fed mantendría sin cambios el costo de los créditos en su próxima reunión del 27 y 28 de octubre. * Los mercados, sin embargo, siguen anticipando que la Fed volvería a subir los tipos de interés hacia finales de año, tras el [USN:L1N4580T6 TEXT:"ajuste de septiembre"], amenazando con reducir el respaldo que el amplio diferencial entre los rendimientos de México y Estados Unidos ha brindado durante años a la [USN:L1N45L0OH TEXT:"divisa mexicana"]. * A nivel local, la minuta de la última reunión de Banco de México mostró recientemente que una parte importante de la [USN:L1N45U0OW TEXT:"Junta de Gobierno"] estaría dispuesta a recortar la tasa clave si mejora el panorama inflacionario. La próxima semana se conocerán las cifras de inflación de la primera quincena de octubre. * En el mercado bursátil, el índice de referencia S&P/BMV IPC (.MXX) subió un 1.87% a 68,929.72 puntos. En la semana, sumó un retorno del 4.36%, su mejor desempeño desde inicios de abril. * Las acciones de la embotelladora y minorista FEMSA (FEMSAUBD.MX) lideraron las alzas de la jornada, con un 5.35% más a 233.70 pesos, después de que [USN:FWN46200B TEXT:"JP Morgan"] elevó su recomendación sobre sus títulos en Nueva York. * Les siguieron los papeles de su unidad Coca-Cola FEMSA (KOFUBL.MX) , la mayor embotelladora de la popular marca en el mundo, que ganaron un 3.62% a 219.43 pesos. * En el mercado de deuda, el banco central colocó 245,546 millones de pesos (13,280 millones de dólares) en una permuta de papel gubernamental.

item.title: US air traffic controllers reach deal with FAA for 2.8% pay rise, WSJ reports
item.description: Air traffic controllers have reached a deal with the FAA for a 2.8% pay increase, the Wall Street Journal reported on Friday, citing people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Air traffic controllers have reached a deal with the FAA for a 2.8% pay increase, the Wall Street Journal reported on Friday, citing people familiar with the matter. In exchange for the pay increase, controllers will now have to badge in and out as a way to prevent early departures from work, the report said. Reuters could not immediately verify the report.

item.title: Judge dismisses child sex abuse charges against actor Timothy Busfield
item.description: A state court judge in New Mexico on Friday dismissed charges of child sexual abuse against "West Wing" actor and director Timothy Busfield, saying the prosecution did not act in a fair and impartial manner during grand jury proceedings.
item.dc:creator: Lisa Richwine
item.content:encoded: A state court judge in New Mexico on Friday dismissed charges of child sexual abuse against "West Wing" actor and director Timothy Busfield, saying the prosecution did not act in a fair and impartial manner during grand jury proceedings. Judge Joseph Montano said prosecutors could pursue new charges against Busfield. The actor has strongly denied allegations of improperly touching two young boys, twin brothers, on the Albuquerque set of Fox TV drama "The Cleaning Lady." A spokesperson for the Second Judicial District Attorney Office of New Mexico said the office was evaluating its options. The twins reported that the alleged contact had occurred over a two-year period, when they were aged 7 and 8, during breaks in production, prosecutors said in a criminal complaint filed in January. Busfield, a director and producer of "The Cleaning Lady," was charged in February[USN:L1N3Z210P TEXT:" in a four-count grand jury indictment "]that accused the actor of groping one of the boys. He steadfastly professed his innocence, calling the allegations against him "lies," and his attorneys asked for the charges against him to be dismissed. In Friday's ruling, Montano said the prosecution did not properly instruct members of the grand jury on procedures for requesting testimony from additional witnesses. In part, the prosecutor incorrectly informed the grand jurors that at least eight of them would have to agree to wanting to hear from a witness for that person to be called. "The prosecuting attorney failed to act in a fair and impartial manner," Montano wrote, adding that the lawyer's actions "had the practical effect of unilaterally withholding witnesses requested by the grand jurors." Busfield, 69, is best known for his prime-time television roles as a White House reporter on the NBC political drama "The West Wing" and as an advertising agency executive on ABC ensemble series "Thirtysomething." He also appeared in the baseball film "Field of Dreams," starring Kevin Costner.

item.title: Brazil may offer credit lines to ease impact of tax, labor reforms, minister says
item.description: Brazil's Finance Minister Dario Durigan said on Friday that specific credit lines could be unveiled by the government for companies affected by a consumer tax reform and the end of the six-day work schedule, which take effect next year.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Brazil's Finance Minister Dario Durigan said on Friday that specific credit lines could be unveiled by the government for companies affected by a consumer tax reform and the [USN:L1N46100U TEXT:"end of the six-day"] work schedule, which take effect next year. In an interview with Band TV, Durigan added that the lines would aim to boost training, innovation, and productivity in the country. Durigan spoke two days after Brazil's Senate approved a constitutional amendment to reduce the country's workweek from six days to five. The new rule will take effect by the end of next year after a 14-month transition, while a consumer tax reform approved in 2023 will also take effect in 2027. The minister acknowledged that some companies will be affected by the labor reform, but said he sees the impact as "minor". "Business owners need government support to be part of this new era," Durigan said. He also said that Brazil's high interest rates remain a problem to be tackled if President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva wins a new term in an presidential runoff later this month. Lula will face Senator Flavio Bolsonaro in a second-round vote on October 25, with the leftist incumbent [USN:L1N461163 TEXT:"currently trailing "]the right-wing lawmaker in polls.

item.title: Boeing sales chief McMullen to retire, company memo says
item.description: Boeing jetliner sales chief Brad McMullen is retiring in December and will be succeeded in one of the industry's most high-profile jobs by Ryan Weir, currently in charge of the North American market, according to a memo seen by Reuters.
item.dc:creator: Tim Hepher
item.content:encoded: Boeing (BA.N) jetliner sales chief Brad McMullen is retiring in December and will be succeeded in one of the industry's most high-profile jobs by Ryan Weir, currently in charge of the North American market, according to a memo seen by Reuters. McMullen, senior vice president of global sales and marketing, led the company's commercial recovery from a 2024 incident involving a mid-air door plug blowout, and was seen as instrumental in soothing concerns from rattled airlines. "Brad has been at the forefront of our efforts to win in the market by developing deep and trusting relationships with our customers," Boeing Commercial Airplanes CEO Stephanie Pope said in the memo. Buoyed by a series of deals coinciding with foreign visits by US President Donald Trump, Boeing won [USN:L6N3YE003 TEXT:"its order race"] against Airbus in 2025 for the first time in seven years, a sign of the nascent turnaround at the US planemaker following back-to-back crises. The company has enjoyed a surge of orders for its 787 wide-body jet but continues to lag Airbus (AIR.PA) in the busy market for long-range narrowbody jets like the A321neo -- a strategic gap it hopes to close with the upcoming approval of its 737 MAX 10. Before running Boeing's North American sales, Weir served as sales chief for Boeing in India and South Asia and took charge of sales to global leasing companies, the memo said.

item.title: SoftBank weighs $18 billion acquisition of Allied Universal, source says
item.description: SoftBank Group is considering an acquisition of Allied Universal in a deal that could value the US security services provider at about $18 billion, a source familiar with the matter said on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Milana Vinn
item.content:encoded: SoftBank Group (9984.T) is considering an acquisition of Allied Universal in a deal that could value the US security services provider at about $18 billion, a source familiar with the matter said on Friday. Allied Universal provides security staffing for businesses, venues and major events, and has a growing presence in the data center industry, supporting both development and operation of facilities The potential acquisition would complement SoftBank founder Masayoshi Son's increasing focus on AI, as he is exploring the use of AI-powered robots across industries, and looking to strengthen the infrastructure needed to support the technology With Allied, SoftBank would look to eventually replace some staff with robots for certain security tasks, though the deployment of humanoid security workers is likely to take longer. Deliberations are preliminary and no final decisions have been made, including on the potential price, Bloomberg News first reported the news SoftBank declined to comment on the report, while Allied Universal did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment SoftBank is widely known for making large technology investments through its Vision Fund. It was an early investor in Alibaba, owns a majority stake in Arm, and was a major backer of the office-sharing startup WeWork The deal builds on SoftBank's broader push into robotics and automation, following its agreement last year to acquire swiss engineering group ABB's robotics business for [USN:FWN3VO2QC TEXT:"$5.4 billion"]

item.title: Court backs EPA giving Oklahoma authority over environmental rules on tribal lands
item.description: A divided federal appeals court on Friday upheld a Trump administration decision to unconditionally grant Oklahoma authority over environmental programs on tribal lands within the state.
item.dc:creator: Nate Raymond
item.content:encoded: A divided federal appeals court on Friday upheld a Trump administration decision to unconditionally grant Oklahoma authority over environmental programs on tribal lands within the state. A 2-1 panel of the Denver-based 10th US Circuit Court of Appeals ruled that the US Environmental Protection Agency acted in accordance with a long-dormant provision in a 2005 transportation funding bill that allows Oklahoma to seek authority over environmental regulatory programs in Native American territory. The provision was dubbed the "Midnight Rider" because it was added late and without discussion to the Safe, Accountable, Flexible, Efficient Transportation Equity Act. Oklahoma did not invoke the provision until 2020, after the US Supreme Court's 5-4 decision in [USN:KBN24A26T TEXT:"McGirt v. Oklahoma"], which recognized about half of Oklahoma — much of the eastern part of the state — as Native American reservation land beyond the jurisdiction of state authorities. Later that year, the EPA during President Donald Trump’s first administration [USN:L1N2GX287 TEXT:"approved"] Oklahoma’s request. At the request of several tribes including the Pawnee Nation, the EPA under Democratic President Joe Biden [USN:L1N2T71U0 TEXT:"withdrew the approval"] in 2021 and reconsidered the matter. In Biden's final days in office, the EPA again approved Oklahoma's request but with a condition that the state engage in efforts to seek consensus with affected tribes. But once Trump returned to the White House, the agency issued a new decision last year eliminating that condition, prompting a lawsuit by the Pawnee Nation. The tribe argued the EPA’s action violated the Administrative Procedure Act, saying the Midnight Rider expired in 2009 along with other parts of the 2005 spending law and that EPA wrongly concluded under Trump that it had no authority to impose conditions when approving Oklahoma's request. But US Circuit Judge Timothy Tymkovich, writing for the majority, said the Midnight Rider contained no sunset provision and did not authorize the Biden-era condition. "Congress’s command that the EPA 'shall approve' a valid request does not authorize the agency to shrink that approval by attaching a condition to it," he wrote. Michael Freeman, a lawyer for Pawnee Nation at Earthjustice, called the ruling disappointing and said his client was considering its options. Tymkovich, who was appointed by Republican President George W. Bush, was joined by US Circuit Judge Robert Bacharach, an appointee of Democratic President Barack Obama. US Circuit Judge Richard Federico, a Biden appointee, dissented, saying the EPA had the discretion to impose at least some protections for tribal interests. "This court should not so readily acquiesce to the total displacement of the tribes as the first sovereigns of their land absent a clear statement from Congress to the contrary," he wrote. The case is Pawnee Nation of Oklahoma v Zeldin, 10th US Circuit Court of Appeals, No. 25-9548. For Pawnee Nation of Oklahoma: Michael Freeman of Earthjustice For the United States: Cameron Hinojos of the US Department of Justice Read more: [USN:L1N2T71U0 TEXT:"EPA withdraws Trump Oklahoma environment order after input from tribes"] [USN:L1N2GX287 TEXT:"Tribes slam EPA move to give Oklahoma control of environmental rules"]

item.title: Top global climate science body suspends meeting without deal on major review timeline
item.description: A meeting of the members of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) was suspended without an agreement on a timeline to publish its next review of the latest science on the warming planet, the IPCC said on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Sudarshan Varadhan
item.content:encoded: A meeting of the members of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) was suspended without an agreement on a timeline to publish its next review of the latest science on the warming planet, the IPCC said on Friday. The [USN:L1N45V07P TEXT:"impasse over the timeline"], which has lasted nearly three years, could leave countries to decide the next phase of climate action without consensus on critical issues, including the extent to which some global warming might be reversible. The meeting was suspended after it ran over its planned duration on the last day and many delegations from least-developed countries and small island states had to leave, the IPCC said in a statement. Agreeing publication dates for its next review of the latest science was the main agenda of the IPCC meeting of 195 member states in the Ethiopian capital Addis Ababa this week. Governments are set to assess progress toward goals set in the [USN:L8N3Z91SG TEXT:"2015 Paris agreement"] at the UN climate talks in November 2028, in a so-called "Global Stocktake". The discussions on the review timeline and the IPCC budget "remain open," and the panel's deliberations will resume at the earliest opportunity, the IPCC said, without providing details. The possibility that the IPCC's reports might not be ready in time for the 2028 climate talks has alarmed a coalition of 30 countries, including European, Latin American and small-island states pushing for immediate action. However, countries including India, Kenya, Saudi Arabia, Russia and China are pressing for more time to prepare the IPCC's next reports to ensure scientists from less-resourced countries can make meaningful contributions. "We were here to work, but found every proposal dismissed — on inclusivity, on the relevance of the science for our national planning, on the necessity of evidence to inform the next Global Stocktake," said Tina Stege, climate envoy for the Marshall Islands. "Progress was blocked, down to the end — a shameful play for time when there is no time to waste." The IPCC's reviews carry weight as they are written by hundreds of international experts and approved by every member state, and are used by governments to plan responses to climate change and cited in international court rulings. The UN Environment Programme has said repeatedly that global efforts to limit warming are falling short and that deeper emissions cuts are needed to avoid climate-related disasters.

item.title: Avenue Capital emerges as frontrunner for stake in Serie A media rights venture, sources say
item.description: Private equity firm Avenue Capital has emerged as the leading bidder for a minority stake in the company that will hold the international media rights of Italy's top soccer league Serie A, two people with knowledge of the matter told Reuters.
item.dc:creator: Elvira Pollina
item.content:encoded: Private equity firm Avenue Capital has emerged as the leading bidder for a minority stake in the company that will hold the international media rights of Italy's top soccer league Serie A, two people with knowledge of the matter told Reuters. Serie A is exploring the sale of a stake in a company that will hold its international broadcasting, sponsorship and betting rights and last month it received final bids from private equity firms . Serie A clubs met on Friday for an initial review of the bids, the two people said. New York-based Avenue Capital is targeting a stake of 10% in the media company for €320 million, the people said, which would put the overall valuation of the venture at €3.2 billion. Avenue is in the lead despite the fact that some rival bidders have offered to pay more because its offer is structured as a common equity investment, without the protections on future cash flows sought by some of the competitors, one of the two people said. The person added that Carlyle and Nextalia, which teamed up to submit a joint bid, had offered around €650 million for a stake of roughly 17%, valuing the venture at about €3.75 billion. The Avenue Capital offer will be examined more closely in the coming weeks by the clubs, the people said, cautioning that there is no final decision on the matter. Avenue Capital and Serie A declined to comment. Carlyle and Nextalia were not immediately available to comment. Any deal requires the backing of at least 14 of the league's 20 clubs. Home to Inter Milan, AC Milan and Juventus (JUVE.MI) , the Italian league has been struggling in recent years to sell its media rights abroad, as broadcasters' interest dwindled due to a crowded fixture list dominated by the expanded UEFA Champions League and the popularity of England's Premier League. The Serie A international media unit generates sales of around €250 million a year, a fraction of those yielded by Premier League and Spain's LaLiga, according to data from European soccer body UEFA.

item.title: Nearly 12,000 California residents bought EVs using state rebate program
item.description: California said on Friday that nearly 12,000 residents bought electric vehicles since August using rebates under a new $270 million program funded by the state and automakers.
item.dc:creator: David Shepardson
item.content:encoded: California said on Friday that nearly 12,000 residents bought electric vehicles since August using rebates under a new $270 million program funded by the state and automakers. Still, overall EV sales have fallen in California and nationwide as President Donald Trump's administration has removed federal incentives for them. EV sales are up globally- fueled by rising oil prices. The program for California residents buying their first EV, which Governor Gavin Newsom signed into law in July, offers $3,500 rebates on new EVs with retail prices of up to $50,000 and a $1,750 rebate for used EVs costing no more than $25,000. California said EVs accounted for 18% of all sales in the state through September 30, down from 23% last year and 25% in 2024. Tesla (TSLA.O) vehicles account for more than half of EVs sold in California. About $70 million has been spent so far with 11,806 new EVs and 132 used EVs purchased — leaving $200 million in rebate funding. The vehicles purchased under the program include 5,658 Tesla, 1,700 Hyundai (005380.KS) , nearly 1,400 Toyota and 1,100 General Motors (GM.N) EVs. Nissan (7201.T) just joined the program and Mitsubishi Motors (7211.T) will begin in November, California said. Other automakers participating in the program are Ford (F.N) , Honda (7267.T) , Kia, Toyota's Lexus brand, Lucid, Rivian (RIVN.O) , Subaru (7270.T) and Volvo. There are no funds remaining for Tesla models under the program, which includes $135.5 million in state funding and $135.5 million from participating automakers. The federal government has dropped support for EVs and charging programs. Trump signed legislation in 2025 that killed the federal $7,500 EV tax credit and the federal $4,000 used-EV credit, which has reduced US sales. California's previous rebate program ended in 2023 and spent $1.49 billion to subsidize 586,000 EV purchases over a decade. Trump has taken aim at EVs on a number of fronts, including signing legislation in June 2025 against California rules, adopted by nearly a dozen other states, that aim to phase out new gasoline-powered cars by 2035. California has sued to challenge the procedure used to reverse the landmark EV rules. The administration has finalized other changes that will save automakers billions of dollars in purchasing credits from Tesla and others to meet prior regulatory requirements.

item.title: Deforestation in Brazil's Amazon falls to all-time low
item.description: Deforestation in Brazil's Amazon rainforest declined to the lowest level on record in the 12 months through July, according to data released by Brazilian space research agency Inpe on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Lisandra Paraguassu, Andre Romani
item.content:encoded: Deforestation in Brazil's Amazon rainforest declined to the lowest level on record in the 12 months through July, according to data released by Brazilian space research agency Inpe on Friday. Some 3,335 square kilometers (1,287.65 square miles) of Amazon jungle were destroyed in the 12 months through July, an all-time low in the historical series that goes back to 1988. It was a fall of about 42% from the preceding period. The previous lowest level for Brazil's Amazon deforestation was reached in 2011-2012, when 4,571 square kilometers were destroyed. In the mid-90s, the figure had reached a record high of nearly 30,000 square kilometers destroyed a year. The data released on Friday, which is produced yearly by Inpe's PRODES satellite monitoring program, is measured from August to July as there is less cloud cover in the middle of the year to obscure deforestation on satellite images. "The figures released today are a historic achievement," said Marcio Astrini, executive secretary at climate advocacy group Observatorio do Clima, adding they show the world that "with political will, it is possible to curb deforestation and greenhouse gas emissions." President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva took office in 2023 [USN:S0N37201F TEXT:"pledging to end deforestation"] by 2030, after it soared to its highest in 15 years during the administration of former President Jair Bolsonaro. Lula will face Bolsonaro's eldest son, Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, in a [USN:S0N45N09L TEXT:"presidential election runoff"] on October 25, after the younger Bolsonaro performed better than expected in the first round. The senator pledged in his manifesto to strengthen environmental oversight in the Amazon, prioritizing areas under the greatest pressure from deforestation and wildfires. He said law enforcement would focus on organized crime rather than on extractive workers and small farmers. In Brazil's Cerrado savanna, deforestation fell about 24% in the period, to some 5,517 square kilometers, also the lowest on record in a series going back to 2001, Inpe data showed.

item.title: Ravens rule out QB Lamar Jackson (ankle) vs. Browns
item.description: Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson will miss his second straight game with an ankle injury on Sunday at Cleveland.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson will miss his second straight game with an ankle injury on Sunday at Cleveland. Tyler Huntley will start under center when the Ravens (4-1) visit the AFC North rival Browns (3-2). Jackson has not practiced since sustaining the injury late in the first half in the Week 4 win against the Tennessee Titans. Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said the decision was the right one for the two-time NFL MVP. "I think it's just a decision for his best interest," the first-year coach said Friday. "That's really what every decision's always going to be about." Jackson, 29, has completed 70.8% of his passes for 967 yards, six touchdowns and one interception in four games this season. He has rushed for 144 yards and one score. Huntley, 28, completed 24 of 32 passes for 201 yards, two touchdowns and no interceptions in last Sunday's 30-23 overtime win at Atlanta. His 1-yard touchdown run in overtime gave Baltimore its third straight win. Also, outside linebacker Trey Hendrickson (finger) will return after missing the past two games. Hendrickson underwent surgery before sitting out the contests. "We're always going to try to have the best interest of the player," Minter said. "The path that we went down was really in (Hendrickson's) best interest, both short-term and long-term. I'm excited for him to be back out there." Center Cam Jurgens (concussion), who was recently acquired from the Philadelphia Eagles, was also ruled out by the Ravens. Defensive tackle Broderick Washington (ankle) will sit out as well. Receiver Ja'Kobi Lane (wrist) returned from injured reserve to practice and is listed as questionable. Also questionable are offensive guards Emery Jones Jr. (ankle) and Andrew Vorhees (foot). --Field Level Media

item.title: White House press secretary Zacharia fired in less than a week after facing criticism
item.description: The departure leaves Trump without a key public messenger just over two weeks before November's midterm elections.
item.dc:creator: Nandita Bose, Trevor Hunnicutt, Jasper Ward
item.content:encoded: White House press secretary [USN:FWN45V14O TEXT:"Katie Zacharia"] was fired after less than a week on the job, two US officials said on Friday, after a rocky start as President Donald Trump 's top spokesperson. Zacharia was "let go" and is "transitioning out" of the press secretary position, according to two separate White House officials. She faced days of questions about her [USN:L6N4601D0 TEXT:"legal credentials"] and criticism of her performance in a news briefing and interviews. The departure leaves Trump without a key public messenger just over two weeks before November's midterm elections , a critical period when the president is seeking to tout his administration's accomplishments and help his fellow Republicans retain control of Congress. Trump told reporters earlier on Friday that he had asked Zacharia to reconsider whether to continue in her role after facing tough press coverage during her first days on the job. "I told her: 'I think you're better off being happy, and I'm not sure you can ever be happy in this stuff.' There's nothing easy about this stuff," Trump told reporters as he departed the White House for a weekend trip. He added: "I said to her honestly, 'If I were you, I'd reconsider... think about it. But I would reconsider.'" Trump said he intended to revisit the conversation with Zacharia later. Zacharia started on Monday and held her debut White House briefing on Tuesday. She said she received a call about the press secretary role on October 7 and was offered the job to succeed [USN:FWN4491F6 TEXT:"Karoline Leavitt"] a week ago. She soon faced questions about her career, which she said included a tenure practicing law. Trump had also described her as an attorney. "I practiced international transaction law, with all the appropriate credentials," Zacharia said in an emailed statement on Wednesday. Reuters could not find records showing the Pepperdine University law school graduate was registered as an attorney or member of the bar in any US state or the District of Columbia. During a Fox News interview on Thursday, Zacharia said she [USN:L1N46201S TEXT:"did not pass the bar"] exam. Law school graduates cannot legally practice law in the US without first being admitted to a state bar. Zacharia and the White House did not immediately respond to an email seeking comment about her firing. Earlier on Friday, she told reporters at the White House that she was looking forward to working with the press. Trump hired Zacharia after expressing concerns about the media coverage of his administration, feeling he needed a new spokesperson who could amplify his achievements, according to two people familiar with the conversations. In a phone interview with Fox on Friday, Trump said he was in no rush to name a new press secretary. Zacharia's quick exit meant she had what is believed to be the shortest tenure of any press secretary in the role's history. "Records are made to be broken," Anthony Scaramucci, who served as director of communications for 10 days during Trump's first administration, said on X. "But I take no pleasure in other people's pain."

item.title: Teacher and armed parent teamed up to stop Oregon school shooter, police say
item.description: The 16-year-old shooter was stopped by a teacher who tackled him and an armed father who fatally shot him, officials said.
item.dc:creator: Deborah Bloom, Herbert Villarraga
item.content:encoded: A 16-year-old boy who shot and killed a teacher and three children in an Oregon special-needs classroom was stopped by another teacher who tackled him and an armed father who fatally shot him, officials said on Friday. Their actions on Thursday saved other lives, the local police chief told a press conference. A day into their investigation of the latest US school shooting, police released new details of the scene at Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, Oregon, where three schoolchildren aged 5, 8 and 11 were killed along with 25-year-old teacher Meghan Lambert. A 7-year-old was wounded and listed in serious but stable condition, and another teacher suffered serious but non-life-threatening injuries, police said. TEACHER 'HELPED PREVENT MORE BLOODSHED,' POLICE SAY The unidentified teacher who stopped the shooter on Thursday threw her phone at him, tackled and fought him. A 36-year-old father of two students then rushed in with a legal .40-caliber pistol and fired at the suspect multiple times, killing him just before police arrived. This teacher, who was not injured, "almost certainly helped prevent more bloodshed," Bend Police Chief Mike Krantz, at times choking back emotion, told a press conference. "The teacher who was willing to stand and fight for her children, that's true heroism," he said, without identifying her. Kenda Freeman told the New York Times that her son Kaylub Giamanco, whose two daughters attend the school, killed the shooter, according to video posted by the New York Times of Freeman reading a brief statement. "He is not seeking recognition but instead wishes to express his gratitude to the first responders, school personnel, and community for the outpouring of love and support," Freeman said, adding that he asked for privacy and did not want to speak to the media. The shooting traumatized much of Bend, a city of about 100,000 people some 175 miles (280 km) southeast of Portland, including 9-year-old fourth-grader Kalani Journeigh and her classmates, who heard the gunshots from a nearby classroom. "All of us were screaming and we were all, like, really scared," Kalani told Reuters, adding that she feared, "We might die." "My heart was beating really fast and after the couple of gunshots that we heard, it just stopped and we never heard it again," she said. A friend of hers was going to get therapy, she said, because "that was really traumatizing to her." Officials identified the shooter as Griffin J. John II, a 16-year-old former special-needs student at the school who was armed with a shotgun. He fired about 15 rounds in the classroom and had another 44 rounds on him, police said. Police were trying to determine what motivated the shooter and how he obtained a Maverick 88 pump-action 12-gauge shotgun, Krantz said. "Everyone wants to know why, including us," the police chief said. "We may never get that full answer, but we want it." VICTIMS MOURNED Just before the shooting, the assailant was seen throwing his weapon over the school fence and then climbing after it onto school grounds. The driver of a truck passing by verbally confronted the boy, who opened fire on the vehicle. The assailant shot through locked glass doors and stormed a class of mixed-grade special-needs students. Police arrived within three minutes of the first call, and the shooter was already dead, Krantz said. People in Bend gathered near the school to mourn on Friday morning, placing flowers and candles outside yellow-crime scene tape that cordoned off the scene. "Thank God for that father," Michael Zappa, 71, who lives just blocks from the school, said through tears. "He saved a lot of lives yesterday, and our prayers should go out for him because he has a lot on his mind today." The family of the slain teacher, Lambert, said working at Silver Rail was a "dream job" for her. "She always fought for the underdog and those with special needs," the family said in a statement that was read aloud at Friday's news conference. Lambert's family also praised Giamanco and expressed gratitude to him. "We think he is a hero," the family said, according to the statement. US school shootings have become more frequent in recent years. Since the start of this year, 118 people have been wounded or killed in 149 incidents involving a gun fired or brandished in a school, or gunshots striking school property, according to the K-12 School Shooting Database, a nonprofit online tracker. A separate online database, the Gun Violence Archive, has recorded 371 mass shootings since January 2026, defining mass shootings as four or more people being struck by gunfire, not including the shooter. Three of those, including the Bend incident, occurred in public schools, the archive said.

item.title: US strikes one-year deal to fund maternal and newborn health donations in poorest countries
item.description: The US government has struck a deal to continue supplying some of the world's poorest nations with free life-saving medication and equipment for mothers, infants and young children, after months of uncertainty and challenges with supply.
item.dc:creator: Ammu Kannampilly, Jennifer Rigby, Victoire Mukenge
item.content:encoded: The US government has struck a deal to continue supplying some of the world's poorest nations with free life-saving medication and equipment for mothers, infants and young children, after [USN:L6N40L0RM TEXT:"months of uncertainty"] and challenges with supply. The UN children's agency UNICEF will now procure these items, a State department spokesperson told Reuters by email, without giving details of the arrangement. UNICEF said the agreement is worth $25 million and will last for one year. That sum represents only a small part of the aid affected by the Trump administration's cuts and dismantling of the US Agency for International Development (USAID). But it means that some of the world's most vulnerable nations will not face another abrupt disruption to supplies they relied on while they work on new health aid deals with the US. Nine former US aid officials, NGOs and government officials told Reuters that this had been a real concern because the deal the now-defunct USAID had with its contractor was due to run out last month. SHORTAGES The agreement covers the procurement and delivery of maternal and child health supplies, as well as some nutrition supplies, to at least 15 countries previously covered, including Democratic Republic of Congo, Haiti and Mali, UNICEF said. It follows almost 18 months of disruption after Washington's move to freeze and then scale back [USN:L2N3PI0VN TEXT:"many US aid programmes"] as part of its "America First Global Health Strategy". In countries such as Congo, shortages due to the disruption have already been showing up on the ground. At the Nyangezi General Hospital in eastern Congo, health workers said they had run out of supplies of life-saving medications including oxytocin to prevent and treat post-partum haemorrhage and amoxicillin, an antibiotic for paediatric use and during childbirth. "It was a donation we received (previously) from USAID, and at the moment, there is none," midwife Alice Bulambo told Reuters. The main government-run warehouse in the area has faced stockouts for over a year, said Olivier Kabarati Amani, chief medical officer for Nyangezi health zone. As a result, facilities are forced to buy medicines at market prices. Over the last six months, "the cost of care has doubled, if not tripled," Amani said, at a time when the healthcare system in eastern Congo is [USN:L6N45L142 TEXT:"already struggling"] with Ebola. The US State Department said it "has prioritized ensuring all life-saving commodities have continued to be made reliably available." TRANSITION Maternal and newborn health items amounted to less than 1% of the more than $5 billion spent by the USAID Global Health Supply Chain program between 2016 and 2023, according to the most recently available annual report. The spending was channelled through private contractor Chemonics. Reuters [USN:L6N40L0RM TEXT:"first reported"] on plans to close this programme, which also managed the donation and delivery of supplies to tackle malaria and HIV, in April, with aid officials warning that the September 30 shutdown could cause shortages. The plans to close the Chemonics supply chain are part of the broader US global health strategy, which aims to move countries towards self-reliance alongside scaled-back US support and reduced reliance on contractors. The US has instead signed more than 30 bilateral deals on health aid with recipient countries, including Congo, which require co-financing from the countries and are worth billions of dollars in total. But the details of the deals are still being worked out and it had been unclear what would fill the gap in the ordering procedure in the meantime. While many nations were already moving towards taking over their maternal and child health needs, lead times for orders can be a year or more, five former USAID officials said. The Congolese government aims to take over by next year, but has struggled with the recent uncertainty, said Polydor Kabila, coordinator of the universal healthcare programme in the president’s office. Alongside the UNICEF deal, the US authorities have extended the deadline for Chemonics deliveries of some key malaria and HIV items, the State Department spokesperson told Reuters. The US has also signed a deal with the Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria to allow countries to order new US-funded HIV and malaria supplies through the Fund's order platform. In a statement, UNICEF said it would work with the US to "keep health and nutrition supplies moving so more children receive life-saving care," adding that no orders have yet been placed but are expected shortly.

item.title: Chinese online retailer Temu agrees to data privacy curbs to settle Texas lawsuit
item.description: Chinese online retailer Temu has agreed to settle data privacy claims raised by Texas and will restrict how it handles personal data from shoppers in the state, according to documents made public on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Jody Godoy, David Shepardson
item.content:encoded: Chinese online retailer Temu has agreed to settle data privacy claims raised by Texas and will restrict how it handles personal data from shoppers in the state, according to documents made public on Friday. Temu faces several lawsuits from US states concerned that the company unlawfully harvests US user data that could be accessed by the Chinese government. Texas is the first to resolve such claims. It is also the first time the company has agreed to keep personal data on US servers and restrict when it can be sent to China, Texas officials said. The company agreed to conduct annual independent product safety testing to identify products containing dangerous chemicals and materials. Temu must remove any products found to contain dangerous materials, terminate the seller and its affiliated stores, notify affected Texas consumers and issue full refunds. Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton said the settlement also requires Temu "to implement rigorous new product audits and safety standards to protect consumers from dangerous materials in products, including clothing and children’s items." He added it will prevent Temu from collecting and using Americans' data. Temu had more than 82.4 million active users in the United States as of September 2023, Paxton's office said. Temu will pay $3 million to the state as part of the settlement and Texas said failure to abide by various data security provisions would result in a potential $8 million penalty each year a violation occurs. Several states sued Temu in the wake of reports alleging Temu and parent company PDD Holdings < PDD.O > used invasive mechanisms in their apps. Temu, which did not admit wrongdoing, said in a statement the company "has come to an agreement to resolve this matter as we continue to focus on serving consumers and supporting businesses across Texas." Under the terms of the settlement, Temu agreed to restrict access to US data necessary to fulfill a transaction, such as shipping addresses, to China. Texas alleged that Temu used code that allows an inappropriate level of access to users’ devices. Temu has denied the allegations.

item.title: US solicits exchange of up to 17 million barrels of oil from strategic reserve
item.description: The United States has issued a request for proposal for an exchange of up to 17 million barrels of crude oil from the nation's Strategic Petroleum Reserve, the Department of Energy said on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The United States has issued a request for proposal for an exchange of up to 17 million barrels of crude oil from the nation's Strategic Petroleum Reserve, the Department of Energy said on Friday. The exchange would be part of a global deal [USN:FWN3ZY1GJ TEXT:"the US struck in March"] to try to control fuel prices impacted by the Iran war . Washington agreed then to loan 172 million barrels of oil from the SPR as part of a wider deal with about 30 countries in the International Energy Agency to release 400 million barrels from reserves around the world. The US has released about 132.5 million barrels from the SPR since the US-Iran war began. The latest 17 million barrel round would be a portion of the pending 40 million barrels of oil that would be the last batch of the release. The Department of Energy had offered the 40 million barrels in June, but revealed later that month that companies agreed to borrow only about 500,000 barrels. The government offered those barrels again in late September. While the Department of Energy has not published the awards from that round, Friday's announcement implies that around 23 million barrels were awarded in the September round, research and consultancy Energy Aspects wrote in a note.

item.title: Panzani, Cerealis in talks to create €1.8 billion European food group
item.description: French pasta maker Panzani and Portugal's Cerealis are in exclusive talks to combine their operations in a deal valuing the merged business at about €1.8 billion ($2.03 billion), they said on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: French pasta maker Panzani and Portugal's Cerealis are in exclusive talks to combine their operations in a deal valuing the merged business at about €1.8 billion ($2.03 billion), they said on Friday. The proposed deal reflects a broader push for consolidation in Europe's food sector as manufacturers seek greater scale to cope with rising costs, strengthen their bargaining power with retailers and expand across regional markets. The deal would create a European food group with about €1 billion in annual revenue and nearly 1,800 employees, the companies said Panzani, which is controlled by private equity firm CVC, generated €620 million of revenue in 2025. Cerealis, controlled by its founding families and Belgian investment company Sofina (SOF.BR) , reported revenue of €400 million Panzani and Cerealis would remain headquartered in Lyon and Porto respectively and retain operational autonomy The merged group would be owned by Cerealis' existing shareholders, including the Moreira da Silva and Silva Domingues families and Sofina, alongside CVC Capital Partners, which would keep a minority stake Cerealis' Executive Vice Chairman Pedro Moreira da Silva would lead the combined group, while Panzani CEO Albert Mathieu would oversee Panzani and its Central European operations. Cerealis CEO Paula Meireles would manage its Iberian and international private-label business ($1 = 0.8887 euros)

item.title: Thousands march in Albanian capital as anti-government protests spread
item.description: Thousands of young Albanians marched through Tirana on Friday, breaking some windows and traffic lights on the fourth day of an increasingly violent student-led campaign to force Prime Minister Edi Rama to resign.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Thousands of young Albanians marched through Tirana on Friday, breaking some windows and traffic lights on the fourth day of an increasingly violent student-led campaign to force Prime Minister Edi Rama to resign. The demonstrations, which are spreading through the country, [USN:L1N4610AQ TEXT:"turned into a riot"] in the capital on Thursday, with protesters smashing windows, raiding a bank and clashing with police. They follow months of mostly peaceful demonstrations that the students say the government ignored. "They are pushing us to the limits," said 19-year-old protester Enea, declining to give a second name for fear of arrest. He said his message to Rama was: "To resign as fast as possible before everything burns down." The students accuse officials of corruption and neglecting education and say they are angry about the sale of pristine parts of Albania's coast to a luxury resort development backed by US President Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner. The unrest is a challenge for Rama, who won a fourth term last year on promises to take Albania into the European Union and is aiming for membership as early as 2028. "We will not bow to violence," he said on Facebook. BUSINESSES APPEAL TO PROTESTERS TO LEAVE THEM ALONE The students, many wearing masks, faced off against lines of riot police in front of the Education Ministry building. Some small businesses had their shutters down and notes on their facades saying: "We are with you. Do not damage our business all over the town." In the coastal town of Lezha, police clashed with stone-hurling protesters. Protests have also spread to Elbasan, Skhodra and Korca, where demonstrators broke windows and set fire to garbage bins, local media reported. "We've been protesting peacefully for 140 days, and nothing was heard. So this is our only chance to be heard and get our rights that we deserve," a 19-year-old protester who gave her name only as Klea said. The demonstrations were sparked by the plans to build the resort, which has faced legal challenges. Villagers told Reuters in July that their land was wrongfully sold for development. Reuters later reported that the man who sold the land was wanted by prosecutors for drug trafficking, charges his lawyer denied. Reuters found no evidence of wrongdoing by Kushner, who is not directly involved in the villagers' dispute. Political analyst Afrim Krasniqi said younger generations saw no future in Albania. "They see that all resources in the country, political resources, economic, everything is in the hands of oligarchs," he told Reuters. Corruption scandals have tarnised Albania's image over the years and analysts say the country is a hub for gangs seeking to launder money from drugs and weapons trafficking, complicating its efforts to join the EU. Along with Montenegro, Albania is leading the accession process among Balkan countries. The unrest is part of a wave of student activism in Europe. In France, high school students [USN:L1N45Z0DG TEXT:"have staged weeks of protests"] and school blockades demanding more teachers and better facilities, arguing that deteriorating school buildings and overcrowded classrooms are undermining education.

item.title: Wall Street tumbles as worries about AI trade and high oil prices weigh
item.description: Wall Street tumbled on Friday, with CoreWeave, Broadcom and other AI-related technology stocks under renewed pressure, while a jump in oil prices spooked traders heading into the weekend.
item.dc:creator: Noel Randewich, Purvi Agarwal
item.content:encoded: Wall Street tumbled on Friday, with CoreWeave, Broadcom and other AI-related technology stocks under renewed pressure, while a jump in oil prices spooked traders heading into the weekend. The Nasdaq was on track for a loss of over 4% for the week, hammered by concerns that debt-laden AI infrastructure companies may not turn profits in time to repay debts, particularly with borrowing costs expected to rise. [USN:L6N4620IB TEXT:"Nvidia-backed"] CoreWeave (CRWV.O) slumped 12%, bringing its loss over the past five sessions to about 25%. The data center operator's bonds also sold off sharply this week, pushing yields above 15%. Broadcom (AVGO.O) fell 3.6%, and the PHLX chip index (.SOX) sank 2.5%, on track for its eighth straight day of declines. Investors on Friday were also watching oil prices jump more than 3% due to Middle East supply worries. "There is some fear in the market," said Rob Haworth, senior investment strategist at U.S. Bank Wealth Management in Seattle. "High oil prices, in particular, tend to weigh on the price/earnings multiple of stocks, and so I think you have investors looking to be cautious into the weekend rather than take more risk." Adding to concerns around AI financing, some current Anthropic investors and prospective investors [USN:L6N4611DN TEXT:"are weighing a lower valuation"] for the company in its upcoming IPO, Reuters reported, citing people familiar with the matter. The S&P 500 was down 1.22% at 7,649.71 points. The Nasdaq declined 2.19% to 26,128.13 points, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average was down 0.55% at 51,891.77 points. Six of the 11 S&P 500 sector indexes declined, led lower by communication services (.SPLRCL) , down 2.52%, followed by a 2.38% loss in information technology (.SPLRCT) . The S&P 500 was set for its steepest weekly loss since January, and the Nasdaq was heading for its sharpest weekly fall since June. Third-quarter earnings season shifts into gear next week with reports from Tesla (TSLA.O) , Meta Platforms (META.O) and Procter & Gamble (PG.N) . Analysts on average see quarterly earnings surging over 30%, driven by AI-related megacaps, according to LSEG data. While the S&P 500 remains up about 12% in 2026, most of that gain has come from AI-related tech stocks, and the index’s median component has climbed only about 6%, year to date. About 185 S&P 500 stocks have lost ground in 2026. Hotter-than-expected consumer and producer inflation reports this week showed price pressures were extending beyond energy commodities. Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh on Friday [USN:L6N462084 TEXT:"voiced optimism"] about US economic strength and surprise about how well global economies have been "hanging in there" during a lingering energy shock and tighter monetary policy to fight inflation. Markets increasingly expect the Fed to keep interest rates unchanged this month. Barclays [USN:FWN4622T4 TEXT:"now expects"] 25-basis-point hikes each in December and January. Tesla (TSLA.O) dropped 2.5% after the electric-vehicle maker unveiled a [USN:L1N46200L TEXT:"redesigned Roadster"], powered by rocket-style thrusters, developed in collaboration with SpaceX. Netflix (NFLX.O) [USN:L4N46128P TEXT:"appointed"] former Disney executive Peter Rice as chief content officer on Thursday. Its shares were down 2.9%. Declining stocks outnumbered rising ones within the S&P 500 (.AD.SPX) by a 1.3-to-one ratio. The S&P 500 posted 19 new highs and one new low; the Nasdaq recorded 49 new highs and 263 new lows. (This story has been corrected to fix the year to 2026 from 2025, in paragraph 13.)

item.title: Huracán Trudy se debilita frente a costas del Pacífico mexicano
item.description: El huracán Trudy se debilitó el viernes en aguas del Pacífico mexicano, pero podría recobrar fuerzas en las próximas horas, advirtieron meteorólogos, mientras continuaba acercándose a la costa occidental del país, que apenas comienza a recuperarse de una serie de ciclones que han dejado inundaciones y daños en semanas recientes.
item.dc:creator: Diego Oré
item.content:encoded: El huracán Trudy se debilitó el viernes en aguas del Pacífico mexicano, pero podría recobrar fuerzas en las próximas horas, advirtieron meteorólogos, mientras continuaba acercándose a la costa occidental del país, que apenas comienza a recuperarse de una serie de ciclones que han dejado inundaciones y daños en semanas recientes. A las 14.00 hora local (2000 GMT), el ciclón se ubicaba a unos 365 kilómetros al suroeste de la ciudad portuaria Acapulco, en el estado Guerrero, y sus vientos máximos sostenidos se habían reducido a 140 kilómetros por hora (km/h), mientras avanzaba hacia el norte-noroeste a 7 km/h, según datos del Centro Nacional de Huracanes de Estados Unidos (NHC, por su sigla en inglés). "Mientras navegaba por las cálidas y tranquilas aguas del Pacífico oriental, Trudy [USN:L6N46119M TEXT:"se fortaleció rápidamente"] el jueves (pero) perdió algo de intensidad de viento durante el viernes", dijo AccuWeather, una compañía estadounidense de servicios comerciales de pronóstico del tiempo. "Trudy seguirá siendo un huracán peligroso mientras se desplaza cerca de la costa centro-occidental de México durante este fin de semana, con fuertes vientos, mar agitado y lluvias torrenciales", agregó. Más temprano, Trudy llegó a ser un huracán de categoría 3 en la escala de Saffir-Simpson y se esperaba que se intensifique a uno de categoría 4. Un ciclón de ese nivel puede soplar vientos máximos sostenidos de hasta 250 km/h y causar daños generalizados en estructuras protectoras, desplome de tejados en edificios pequeños, erosión de bancales y playas e inundaciones en terrenos interiores. Si bien no se prevé que toque tierra, el ciclón, de categoría 1, descargará lluvias torrenciales y dejará fuertes ráfagas de viento y oleaje peligroso en la franja costera que va desde el conocido destino turístico Acapulco hasta Puerto Vallarta, pasando por los dos mayores puertos del país: Manzanillo y Lázaro Cárdenas, puerta de entrada principal para mercancías provenientes de Asia. La agencia de protección civil de México pidió a los residentes que comenzaran a prepararse para la llegada de la tormenta asegurando puertas y ventanas, y retirando objetos que pudieran ser arrastrados por los fuertes vientos. En Acapulco, una ciudad de unos 700,000 habitantes, los pescadores guardaron sus embarcaciones luego que autoridades cerraron algunos puertos pesqueros y turísticos a la navegación de embarcaciones menores. En las últimas semanas, la costa del Pacífico mexicano ha sido golpeada por los huracanes [USN:L6N45L0YK TEXT:"Polo"] y [USN:L8N45V0SM TEXT:"Simon"], y la tormenta Rachel. A causa de las lluvias y las inundaciones, ocho personas perdieron la vida en la ciudad costera de Ensenada, en el estado Baja California. Simon sigue activo, aunque como tormenta tropical, frente a la costa centroccidental del país.

item.title: Russian attacks kill eight in Ukraine, cut power to over a million
item.description: Russian attacks killed at least eight people and injured 60 across Ukraine on Friday, hit two shopping centres and cut power to more than 1 million people after strikes on the energy grid, officials said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Russian attacks killed at least eight people and injured 60 across Ukraine on Friday, hit two shopping centres and cut power to more than 1 million people after strikes on the energy grid, officials said. A 71-year-old woman and a 58-year-old man died and 12 more people were wounded in attacks on three districts of the eastern city of Kharkiv, Governor Oleh Syniehubov said. He had earlier put the death toll at three. Further Russian strikes through the evening injured nine people, officials said. Attacks in the frontline city of Kramatorsk in Donetsk Region killed two people and two more were killed in southeastern Dnipropetrovsk Region. Ukraine's energy ministry said its repair crews had returned power to over 1 million people who had lost it as a result of Russian attacks on Friday. It was not clear how many were still without power. In the northwestern region of Volyn, which borders Poland, a drone strike on a food-processing facility killed one person and wounded eight others, according to Governor Roman Romaniuk. He said 370,000 people were temporarily without power in the morning, although 100,000 of them got supply back later on. The blackout could last for at least 24 hours in Volyn's regional capital, Lutsk, Mayor Andriy Razumovskyi said on Facebook. Romaniuk said that drone attacks continued throughout the day, striking a customs terminal and torching about 10 trucks in the town of Kovel, which sits on a major trunk road from Kyiv to Poland. Other attacks hit at least two shopping centres — one in the northern city of Sumy, which lies close to the front line, and one in the neighbouring region of Rivne, officials said — the latest in a spate of Russian assaults on malls and markets. Pictures from emergency services in Sumy showed blood spattered across the floor and shots of the centre's damaged entrance. One person was killed and seven wounded by drones that hit a major shopping centre and other sites in Rivne, regional governor Oleksandr Koval said. Ukraine's energy ministry said large parts of the city of Rivne and the surrounding area were without power after attacks on energy infrastructure there.

item.title: Hurricane Trudy weakens but may regain strength off Mexican coast
item.description: Hurricane Trudy weakened on Friday but could regain strength in the coming hours, meteorologists warned, as the storm approached Mexico's western coast, packing winds of up to 140 km per hour (85 mph).
item.dc:creator: Diego Oré, Aida Pelaez-fernandez
item.content:encoded: Hurricane Trudy weakened on Friday but could regain strength in the coming hours, meteorologists warned, as the storm approached Mexico's western coast, packing winds of up to 140 km per hour (85 mph). Further strengthening is forecast before Trudy nears Jalisco and Colima states in central-western Mexico late on Saturday as a life-threatening major hurricane, Mexican authorities and the US-based National Hurricane Center said. The center of Trudy will approach the coast of southwestern and west-central Mexico on Saturday and pass near the coast Saturday night into Sunday, the NHC said in its latest advisory. "Trudy will remain a dangerous hurricane as it moves near Mexico's central-western coast this weekend, bringing strong winds, rough seas, and torrential rain," said private forecaster AccuWeather. Earlier, Trudy had reached Category 3 and was expected to intensify to a Category 4 hurricane. Any change in its path closer to shore will increase the severity of its impact, the head of Mexico's weather agency, Fabian Vazquez, said at a press conference. "Everyone in this region needs to be very careful and stay alert over the weekend," he added. Mexico's civil protection agency asked residents to prepare by securing doors and windows, and removing objects that could be thrown around by the strong winds. In the coastal resort city of Acapulco, fishermen pulled their boats ashore after authorities closed some fishing and tourist ports to small vessels. The storm is expected to produce up to 15 inches (38 cm) of rain in the states of Michoacan, Colima and Jalisco, increasing the risk of life-threatening flooding and landslides, according to the NHC. Mexico's Pacific coast has already been battered in recent weeks by storms that left several dead and caused severe flooding. Tropical Storm Simon continues to weaken farther northwest offshore, after [USN:L1N45Y0H6 TEXT:"dropping heavy rain"] along the coast earlier as a hurricane. Last week, Tropical Storm Rachel hit the Baja California peninsula, damaging some 1,500 homes.

item.title: Wall St Week Ahead As AI rally wobbles, stock market's spotlight turns to earnings
item.description: Stumbles in the market-leading AI trade are set to test investor confidence in the rally in the coming week as Wall Street focuses on quarterly results due from key players including Meta Platforms .
item.dc:creator: Lewis Krauskopf
item.content:encoded: Stumbles in the market-leading AI trade are set to test investor confidence in the rally in the coming week as Wall Street focuses on quarterly results due from key players including Meta Platforms (META.O) . AI-linked stocks, central to [USN:L6N45R12W TEXT:"the bull market"] that just marked its fourth anniversary, [USN:L6N460140 TEXT:"struggled in recent days"], with sharp declines in shares of semiconductor companies and tech hardware firms such as Dell Technologies (DELL.N) . Meta, among the hyperscalers spending massively to build AI data centers, highlights the upcoming week of quarterly reports, along with semiconductor firms Lam Research (LRCX.O) and Texas Instruments (TXN.O) and Elon Musk -led companies SpaceX (SPCX.O) and Tesla (TSLA.O) . "It certainly feels like the narrative in the market is a little bit jittery," said Garrett Melson, portfolio strategist with Natixis Investment Managers Solutions. "Clearly there's a lot of uncertainty around where AI stands right now." Worries rippled through markets over risks tied to [USN:L6N461185 TEXT:"the financing of the AI build-out boom"], which has lifted profits for a wide swath of companies and boosted economic growth. Investors were watching [USN:L4N461208 TEXT:"developments with CoreWeave"] (CRWV.O) , an AI cloud company with about $50 billion in debt. This week, its shares tumbled. In other recent signs of caution, strategists at Deutsche Bank and RBC Capital Markets separately pulled back on their recommendations of the tech sector. On October 9, Deutsche Bank strategists said the rotation into tech had "run far and the risk-reward no longer looks favorable in the near term." Dragged down by the swoon in heavyweight tech and AI stocks, the S&P 500 (.SPX) posted its biggest weekly drop since June. But the benchmark index was only about 2% below its record high set this month. Other sectors, which lagged as tech shined last month, posted solid gains on the week, including healthcare and consumer staples. "This is very much an on-off switch type of market," Melson said. "When AI is working, it sucks all the oxygen out of the room for the rest of the sectors." META KICKS OFF HYPERSCALER RESULTS US reporting season heats up next week, with investors counting on robust performance. S&P 500 companies are expected to have increased earnings by more than 30% in the third quarter, according to LSEG IBES. Massive outlays on AI data centers and infrastructure underpin the profit jump. Meta is one of five AI hyperscalers that combined are expected to increase their capital spending to about $1.2 trillion next year, according to Goldman Sachs. Investors are eager for signs the companies can show returns on the investments, which would build confidence that the spending is sustainable. "One of the most important takeaways of earnings season is whether or not the profitability of the hyperscalers can grow faster than the pace of their capex," said Kevin Shea, senior equity analyst at BNY Wealth. Shares of Meta, whose market capitalization was about $1.8 trillion, have risen in recent weeks as it launched its Muse AI assistant "With the cost of capital going up, this capex blowout is going to become more expensive, which raises the bar for returns," said Chuck Carlson, chief executive officer at Horizon Investment Services. "Meta is going to be the first up to try to provide some color around that question." SEMIS, TESLA, NETFLIX ALSO ON TAP Chip companies have been among the biggest beneficiaries of the capital spending boom, but the stocks have cooled off. The Philadelphia SE Semiconductor index (.SOX) has slumped about 12% this month, although it remained up 57% on the year, compared with a roughly 12% year-to-date gain for the S&P 500. Wednesday's reports from Lam Research and Texas Instruments could offer broader indications of demand in the semiconductor industry. Lam Research shares are up 54% in 2026, while Texas Instruments stock is up 59%. Elsewhere, investors will focus on results from Musk-run companies with market values well over $1 trillion: SpaceX — the newly public space company that also has an AI business — and Tesla, another signature stock of the tech-driven bull market. Streaming company Netflix (NFLX.O) , consumer products company Procter & Gamble (PG.N) and engine maker GE Aerospace (GE.N) are among other high-profile reports in the coming week. The rise in Treasury yields and prospects for further rate hikes from the Federal Reserve also remain front-burner issues for stock investors. Hot inflation data this week boosted bets on another rate increase at the Fed's meeting at the end of October. Futures pricing suggested most investors still expect the US central bank to wait until its meeting in December to raise rates for a second time this year. "Another strong earnings season should help equities withstand moderately higher rates," analysts at UBS Global Wealth Management said in a note on Thursday.

item.title: UK clears Axel Springer takeover of Telegraph newspaper group
